docs.title: Mesh Processing
docs.text:
mesh_processing: Triangle mesh operations: subdivision, simplification, and conversion to point clouds via uniform or Poisson-disk sampling.

Methods subdivision, simplification, mesh_to_pcd_uniform, mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk Input files .ply, .obj, .stl, .off Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_objaverse_glb_shard Example Gaussian splats on the Stanford bunny CLI pardesline run mesh_processing.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Mesh processing operates on triangle meshes \(\mathcal{M} = (V, F)\). Key operations include:

Subdivision increases mesh resolution by splitting triangles. Midpoint subdivision inserts new vertices at edge midpoints, quadrupling the face count per iteration.

Simplification reduces complexity using Quadric Error Metrics (QEM) which iteratively collapses edges minimizing \(\Delta(v) = v^T Q v\).

Mesh-to-Point-Cloud sampling converts surfaces to point sets via uniform or Poisson-disk sampling.

docs.title: subdivision
docs.text:
Midpoint subdivision splits each edge at its midpoint creating 4 new triangles from each original. After \(k\) iterations: \(|F| \cdot 4^k\) faces.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("mesh_processing.subdivision")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.mesh_processing.subdivision --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it iterations int 1 1 to 4 Number of subdivision iterations. 1 iteration quadruples the triangle count; two or more are rarely needed before smoothing and make files large quickly.

docs.title: simplification
docs.text:
Quadric Error Metrics decimation collapses edges in order of increasing cost \(v^T (Q_a + Q_b) v\) until the target triangle count is reached.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("mesh_processing.simplification")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `mesh.decimate()`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.mesh_processing.simplification --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh uses the PyVista decimation instead); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it target_triangles int 5000 100 to 100000 Target number of triangles. 5 000 triangles is the size at which an organ or part surface still looks right on screen and loads instantly in a viewer; raise it for metrology. maximum_error (advanced) float 1e+30 0.0 to 1e+30 Advisory maximum quadric error allowed per edge collapse (very large = unbounded, matches default behavior). Unbounded (1e30) matches Open3D's behaviour: the decimation stops at the triangle budget, not at an error threshold, so the result is predictable in size. boundary_weight (advanced) float 1.0 0.0 to 100.0 Weight applied to boundary edges during decimation. 1.0 treats boundary edges like interior ones; raise it on open meshes (scans with holes) so the boundary does not shrink.

docs.title: mesh_to_pcd_uniform
docs.text:
Points are sampled uniformly, each triangle receiving samples proportional to its area \(A_i\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_uniform")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_uniform --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny (examples/points_to_gaussians_bunny); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it num_points int 5000 100 to 100000 Number of points to sample. 5 000 points keep registration and clustering fast while covering a surface; the examples use 20 000-50 000 for visual density. use_triangle_normal (advanced) bool false Assign each sampled point the normal of its source triangle instead of an interpolated vertex normal. Off: interpolated vertex normals are smoother on organic surfaces; turn on for CAD meshes with flat faces. seed (advanced) int -1 -1 to 2147483647 Random seed for sampling (-1 = nondeterministic). -1 (non-deterministic) is Open3D's default; set a seed when a result must be reproducible, as the examples do.

docs.title: mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk
docs.text:
Blue-noise sampling where no two samples are closer than minimum distance \(r\), producing more uniform coverage.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `mesh.to_points(num_points=...)`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny, examples/icp_registration_bunny); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it num_points int 5000 100 to 100000 Approximate number of points. 5 000 is the approximate count after elimination: Poisson-disk sampling gives evenly spaced points, which is what registration features and PointNet training want. init_factor (advanced) int 5 1 to 20 Initial uniform-sample oversampling factor before elimination. 5x oversampling before elimination is Open3D's recommendation: enough candidates for an even blue-noise distribution without a long elimination pass. use_triangle_normal (advanced) bool false Assign each sampled point the normal of its source triangle instead of an interpolated vertex normal. Off: interpolated normals; on for flat-faced CAD meshes. seed (advanced) int -1 -1 to 2147483647 Random seed for sampling (-1 = nondeterministic). -1 is non-deterministic; the examples pass seed=1 for reproducible figures.

docs.title: Point Cloud Processing
docs.text:
point_cloud_processing: Fundamental point cloud operations: downsampling, filtering, outlier removal. Essential preprocessing for all 3D computer vision pipelines.

Methods voxel_downsample, statistical_outlier_removal, radius_outlier_removal, mesh_to_pointcloud Input files .ply, .pcd, .txt, .xyz Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats Example Poisson reconstruction on the Stanford bunny CLI pardesline run point_cloud_processing.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Point cloud processing encompasses the fundamental operations needed to prepare raw 3D data for downstream tasks. A point cloud \(P = \{p_1, \ldots, p_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^3\) often contains noise, outliers, and redundant points.

Voxel downsampling divides the space into a regular grid of cubes (voxels) with side length \(v\) and replaces all points within each voxel by their centroid:

\[ \bar{p}_k = \frac{1}{|V_k|} \sum_{p_i \in V_k} p_i \]

Statistical outlier removal computes the mean distance \(\mu_i\) from each point to its \(k\) nearest neighbors and removes points where \(\mu_i > \bar{\mu} + \alpha \cdot \sigma\).

Radius outlier removal removes points that have fewer than \(n_{\min}\) neighbors within a sphere of radius \(r\).

docs.title: voxel_downsample
docs.text:
Voxel downsampling partitions \(\mathbb{R}^3\) into a regular grid of cubes with side length \(v\). For each non-empty voxel \(V_k\), a representative point is computed as the centroid:

\[\bar{p}_k = \frac{1}{|V_k|} \sum_{p_i \in V_k} p_i\]

This reduces the point count while providing uniform spatial sampling.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.downsample(voxel_size=...)`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny (0.15 m, examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny), KITTI sweeps (metres, examples/kitti_lidar_ground_and_objects); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it voxel_size float 0.02 0.001 to 0.5 Size of each voxel cube. Smaller = more detail. 0.02 in file units: on a metre-scale object or room it keeps one point per 2 cm, enough for registration features and clustering; set it to 2-5x the point spacing of your scanner (0.5 mm for CBCT, 0.1 m for outdoor LiDAR), because the value is absolute, not relative to the object.

docs.title: statistical_outlier_removal
docs.text:
For each point \(p_i\), compute the mean distance to its \(k\) nearest neighbors: $\(\mu_i = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{j=1}^{k} \|p_i - p_{nn_j}\|\)$

A point is classified as an outlier if \(\mu_i > \bar{\mu} + \alpha \cdot \sigma\) where \(\alpha\) is the standard deviation multiplier.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_processing.statistical_outlier_removal")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.clean()`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_processing.statistical_outlier_removal --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny with 0.5 % Gaussian noise (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny, examples/icp_registration_bunny); generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it nb_neighbors int 20 5 to 100 Number of nearest neighbors to consider. 20 neighbours give a stable mean distance per point on scans of 10k-1M points; fewer makes the estimate noisy, more blurs the boundary between surface and stray points. std_ratio float 2.0 0.5 to 5.0 Standard deviation multiplier threshold. 2.0 removes points whose mean neighbour distance is beyond two standard deviations: on scanner noise this drops the flying pixels and keeps thin structures; lower to 1.0 on very noisy depth-camera data, raise to 3.0 on clean CAD-derived clouds. print_progress (advanced) bool false Print a progress bar during removal. Off: the progress bar writes to the terminal and is useless in a pipeline or an agent run.

docs.title: radius_outlier_removal
docs.text:
For each point \(p_i\), count the number of neighbors within radius \(r\). A point is removed if it has fewer than \(n_{\min}\) neighbors.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_processing.radius_outlier_removal")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_processing.radius_outlier_removal --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it radius float 0.05 0.001 to 1.0 Search radius for counting neighbors. 0.05 in file units: a point with fewer than min_neighbors within 5 cm is isolated on a metre-scale scan; scale with the point spacing (about 10x the spacing). min_neighbors int 5 1 to 50 Minimum neighbors required to keep a point. 5 is low enough to keep edges and thin parts, where neighbourhoods are naturally sparse, while isolated speckle has 0-2 neighbours. print_progress (advanced) bool false Print a progress bar during removal. Off: terminal output only.

docs.title: mesh_to_pointcloud
docs.text:
1. Vertex Extraction A triangle mesh \(\mathcal{M} = (V, F)\) consists of a vertex set \(V = \{v_1, \ldots, v_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^3\) and a face set \(F \subset V \times V \times V\). Converting to a point cloud simply discards the connectivity \(F\), retaining only the vertex positions: $\(P = \{v_i \in \mathbb{R}^3 : v_i \in V\}\)$

2. Attribute Preservation Per-vertex attributes (normals \(\vec{n}_i\), colors \(c_i\)) are preserved during conversion. Normals computed from mesh faces remain valid as point normals.

3. Use Cases Useful as a preprocessing step when algorithms require point cloud input (e.g., registration, segmentation) but the source data is a mesh.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_processing.mesh_to_pointcloud")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_processing.mesh_to_pointcloud --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny and armadillo (Open3D data); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

No tunable parameters.

docs.title: Surface Reconstruction
docs.text:
point_cloud_reconstruction: Convert a point cloud into a surface mesh using various reconstruction algorithms: Convex Hull, Alpha Shape, Ball Pivoting, Poisson.

Methods poisson, convex_hull, alpha_shape, ball_pivoting Input files .ply, .pcd, .txt, .xyz Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats Example Poisson reconstruction on the Stanford bunny CLI pardesline run point_cloud_reconstruction.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Surface reconstruction converts a discrete set of 3D points \(P = \{p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n\} \subset \mathbb{R}^3\) into a continuous surface \(S\), typically represented as a triangle mesh \(\mathcal{M} = (V, F)\).

The reconstruction problem is inherently ill-posed: infinitely many surfaces can interpolate a finite point set. Each algorithm introduces different priors: - Convexity (Convex Hull) - Scale-dependent connectivity (\(\alpha\)-shapes, Ball Pivoting) - Smoothness (Poisson reconstruction)

The quality of reconstruction depends on point density, noise level, and the presence of oriented normals \(\{\vec{n}_i\}\) at each sample point.

docs.title: poisson
docs.text:
1. Indicator Function Given oriented point samples \((p_i, \vec{n}_i)\), the Poisson approach defines a vector field \(\vec{V}\) from the normals and seeks an indicator function \(\chi: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}\) whose gradient approximates \(\vec{V}\): $\(\nabla \chi \approx \vec{V}\)$

2. Poisson Equation Applying divergence to both sides yields the Poisson equation: $\(\Delta \chi = \nabla \cdot \vec{V}\)$ This is solved using an adaptive octree of depth \(d\) (the depth parameter), where higher depth captures finer geometric detail.

3. Surface Extraction The iso-surface is extracted at an appropriate level of \(\chi\) using marching cubes. The scale parameter controls the extent of the reconstruction volume relative to the bounding box of the input samples.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_reconstruction.poisson")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.to_mesh()`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_reconstruction.poisson --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny sampled to 20 000 points (examples/poisson_reconstruction_bunny); ultrasound and CBCT reconstructions in the atlas-label-transfer and pointnet-segmentation skills; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it depth int 9 4 to 13 Octree depth. Higher = more detail but slower. 9 gives 512 cells across the bounding cube: on 20k-200k point scans it recovers organ- and part-level detail without fitting the noise; 8 is Open3D's default and blurs small features, 10-11 need hundreds of thousands of points. scale float 1.1 0.5 to 2.0 Ratio between reconstruction cube and samples bounding cube. 1.1 is the Kazhdan reference setting: the reconstruction cube is 10 % larger than the samples' bounding cube so the surface can close outside the data. width (advanced) float 0.0 0.0 to 1.0 Target finest octree cell width; 0 uses depth instead. 0 means depth drives the resolution; set a width in file units when you know the target cell size (e.g. 1 mm). linear_fit (advanced) bool false Use linear interpolation to estimate iso-vertex positions. Off: the default iso-vertex placement is smoother; linear fit is faster and slightly blockier. n_threads (advanced) int -1 -1 to 64 Number of threads (-1 = all available). -1 uses every core. density_quantile (advanced) float 0.01 0.0 to 1.0 Density quantile below which low-support vertices are removed as noise. 0.01 removes the 1 % of vertices with the least sample support: that is where Poisson balloons over holes and partial views, so the output is a clean, density-trimmed surface rather than a bubble; raise to 0.05-0.1 on very partial scans. normal_radius (advanced) float 0.1 0.001 to 10.0 Search radius for normal estimation when the cloud has no normals. 0.1 in file units for normal estimation when the cloud has none; about 5-10x the point spacing on metre-scale data, scale it for millimetre scans. normal_max_nn (advanced) int 30 1 to 200 Max neighbours for normal estimation when the cloud has no normals. 30 neighbours is enough for a stable covariance; more smooths sharp edges. normal_orient_k (advanced) int 15 1 to 200 k for consistent tangent-plane normal orientation. 15 neighbours for consistent orientation: Poisson needs normals pointing the same way, and a small k keeps the propagation local on thin parts.

docs.title: convex_hull
docs.text:
1. Definition The convex hull \(\text{CH}(P)\) is the smallest convex polytope containing all points: $\(\text{CH}(P) = \left\{ \sum_{i=1}^{n} \lambda_i p_i : \lambda_i \geq 0, \sum_i \lambda_i = 1 \right\}\)$

2. Complexity Computed in \(O(n \log n)\) using the Quickhull algorithm. The output mesh has at most \(2n - 4\) triangular faces.

3. Limitations Cannot represent concavities — the result is always a convex polytope. Best suited for convex objects or as a bounding approximation.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_reconstruction.convex_hull")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_reconstruction.convex_hull --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it joggle_inputs (advanced) bool false Randomly perturb inputs to avoid QHull errors on coplanar/degenerate points. Off: exact hull; turn on only when QHull fails on coplanar or duplicated points.

docs.title: alpha_shape
docs.text:
1. Generalized Hull Alpha shapes generalize convex hulls by introducing a scale parameter \(\alpha > 0\). A Delaunay simplex (triangle) is included in the alpha shape if it can be circumscribed by a sphere of radius \(r \leq 1/\alpha\).

2. Scale Behavior - \(\alpha \to 0\): the alpha shape approaches the point set itself - \(\alpha \to \infty\): the alpha shape approaches the convex hull - Intermediate \(\alpha\): captures concavities at scale \(\sim 1/\alpha\)

3. Topological Properties Alpha shapes can produce surfaces with holes, disconnected components, and non-manifold edges depending on point density and \(\alpha\) value.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_reconstruction.alpha_shape")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_reconstruction.alpha_shape --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it alpha float 0.03 0.005 to 0.5 Alpha parameter. Smaller = tighter fit (more detail). Larger = smoother. 0.03 in file units is a tight fit on metre-scale objects with centimetre point spacing; alpha must be larger than the largest gap you want bridged and smaller than the smallest concavity you want kept.

docs.title: ball_pivoting
docs.text:
1. Algorithm Ball Pivoting (Bernardini et al., 1999) rolls a ball of radius \(\rho\) over the point cloud. Starting from a seed triangle formed by three mutually tangent points, the ball pivots around each edge, adding triangles when it contacts a new point.

2. Multi-Scale Reconstruction Using multiple radii \(\{\rho, 2\rho, 4\rho\}\) captures geometry at different scales. The radius_factor parameter sets \(\rho\) as a multiple of the average nearest-neighbor distance: $\(\rho = f \cdot \bar{d}_{\text{nn}}\)$

3. Requirements Requires oriented normals \(\vec{n}_i\) to determine the inside/outside of the surface. Works best with uniformly sampled, noise-free point clouds.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_reconstruction.ball_pivoting")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_reconstruction.ball_pivoting --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it radius_factor float 2.0 0.5 to 10.0 Ball radius as factor of average point spacing. Uses multiple radii (1x, 2x, 4x). 2x the average point spacing is the smallest ball that rolls over a sampled surface without falling through; the multi-scale set (1x, 2x, 4x) then fills the larger gaps. radii_multipliers (advanced) list 1,2,4 CSV of base-radius multipliers defining the multi-scale ball set. 1,2,4 is the classic multi-scale schedule: small balls first for detail, larger ones to bridge sparse regions. normal_radius (advanced) float 0.1 0.001 to 10.0 Search radius for normal estimation when the cloud has no normals. 0.1 in file units for normal estimation when the cloud has none. normal_max_nn (advanced) int 30 1 to 200 Max neighbours for normal estimation when the cloud has no normals. 30 neighbours for a stable covariance. normal_orient_k (advanced) int 15 1 to 200 k for consistent tangent-plane normal orientation. 15 for consistent orientation; ball pivoting needs oriented normals.

docs.title: Point Cloud Segmentation
docs.text:
point_cloud_segmentation: Segment a point cloud into meaningful regions using geometric methods: RANSAC plane fitting and DBSCAN clustering.

Methods ransac_plane, dbscan_clustering Input files .ply, .pcd, .txt, .xyz Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats CLI pardesline run point_cloud_segmentation.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Point cloud segmentation partitions a set of 3D points \(P = \{p_1, \ldots, p_n\}\) into disjoint subsets corresponding to semantic or geometric regions.

RANSAC-based plane fitting iteratively fits a plane model \(\vec{n} \cdot \vec{x} + d = 0\) to random point subsets.

DBSCAN groups points based on density: a point is a core point if it has at least \(n_{\min}\) neighbors within radius \(\epsilon\).

docs.title: ransac_plane
docs.text:
RANSAC iteratively fits a plane model and identifies inliers within distance threshold \(\epsilon\). Plane inliers are colored distinctly from outliers.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_segmentation.ransac_plane")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_segmentation.ransac_plane --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; the same RANSAC plane model runs on KITTI in lidar_scene_detection

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it distance_threshold float 0.01 0.001 to 0.1 Maximum distance from point to plane for inlier. 0.01 in file units: one centimetre on metre-scale indoor scans, which is the depth-camera noise level; use 0.2-0.3 m for outdoor LiDAR ground. num_iterations int 1000 100 to 10000 Number of RANSAC iterations. 1 000 iterations find the dominant plane with probability above 0.99 when it holds at least 20 % of the points. ransac_n (advanced) int 3 3 to 10 Number of points sampled to estimate each plane candidate. 3 points define a plane; the minimum keeps the inlier probability per draw highest. probability (advanced) float 0.99999999 0 to 1 Expected probability of finding the best plane (early-stop confidence). 0.99999999 lets Open3D stop early once the best plane is almost certainly found, so the 1 000 iterations are a ceiling.

docs.title: dbscan_clustering
docs.text:
DBSCAN groups points based on density. Given parameters \((\epsilon, n_{\min})\), connected core points form clusters. Each cluster gets a unique color.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("point_cloud_segmentation.dbscan_clustering")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.segment(eps=..., min_points=...)`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.point_cloud_segmentation.dbscan_clustering --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py; KITTI sweeps through lidar_scene_detection.object_clustering

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it eps float 0.02 0.001 to 0.5 Maximum distance between two points in same cluster. 0.02 in file units: two centimetres joins points of the same object on indoor depth scans; use 0.5 m outdoors (see object_clustering). min_points int 10 3 to 100 Minimum points to form a cluster. 10 points keep speckle out of the cluster list while small objects (a cup, a hand) still form one. print_progress (advanced) bool false Print an Open3D progress bar during clustering. Off: terminal output only.

docs.title: PyVista Analysis
docs.text:
pyvista_analysis: Geometric analysis and attribute computation via PyVista: curvature estimation, distance computation, glyph generation, vector magnitude, and scalar statistics.

Methods pv_curvature, pv_distance, pv_glyph, pv_vector_magnitude, pv_scalar_stats, pv_extract_feature_edges Input files .ply, .obj, .stl, .vtk, .vtu Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_objaverse_glb_shard CLI pardesline run pyvista_analysis.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
PyVista analysis tools compute derived geometric quantities:

Curvature estimates surface curvature (mean, Gaussian, min, max) at each vertex. Distance computes point-to-surface distances between two meshes. Glyphs visualize vector fields by placing oriented symbols at data points. Vector Magnitude computes \(\|\mathbf{v}\|\) for each vector in a field. Scalar Statistics provides summary statistics of scalar arrays.

docs.title: pv_curvature
docs.text:
Curvature types: mean \(H = \frac{\kappa_1 + \kappa_2}{2}\), Gaussian \(K = \kappa_1 \kappa_2\), maximum \(\kappa_1\), minimum \(\kappa_2\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_curvature")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.curvature --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it curvature_type string mean Curvature type: mean, gaussian, maximum, or minimum. mean curvature is the one that reads as 'bumps and dents' on an organ or a part; Gaussian separates saddles, maximum/minimum are the principal curvatures.

docs.title: pv_distance
docs.text:
Computes the closest-point distance from each vertex to a reference surface using a KD-tree.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_distance")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.distance --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

No tunable parameters.

docs.title: pv_glyph
docs.text:
Creates oriented arrow glyphs at each point, scaled by a factor and oriented along a vector field.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_glyph")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.glyph --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it scale_factor float 0.01 0.0001 to 1.0 Scale factor for glyph size. 0.01 in file units draws normal arrows of 1 % of a unit object, visible without hiding the surface. vector_name string Normals Vector array to orient glyphs (e.g. Normals). Normals is the array every mesh has after compute_normals. scale (advanced) bool false Scale glyphs by scalar/vector magnitude. Off: all arrows the same length, so direction is what you see. tolerance (advanced) float -1.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Merge tolerance as fraction of bbox (-1 = auto/None). -1 lets PyVista choose the glyph merge tolerance. absolute (advanced) bool false Interpret tolerance as an absolute distance. Off: the tolerance is a fraction of the bounding box. clamping (advanced) bool false Clamp glyph scaling to the rng range. Off: no scaling range clamp since scale is off.

docs.text:
Computes \(\|\mathbf{v}_i\| = \sqrt{v_{ix}^2 + v_{iy}^2 + v_{iz}^2}\) for each vector and stores as a scalar.

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_vector_magnitude")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.vector_magnitude --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it vector_name string Normals Name of the vector array to compute magnitude for. Normals is the array every mesh has.

docs.title: pv_scalar_stats
docs.text:
Computes min, max, mean, median, std, and stores a normalized version of the scalar array.

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_scalar_stats")  # catalog defaults

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.scalar_stats --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it scalars string "" Scalar array name (empty = first available). Empty takes the first available array.

docs.title: pv_extract_feature_edges
docs.text:
Extracts edges where the surface normal changes sharply. A feature edge is identified when the dihedral angle between adjacent faces exceeds the threshold. Also detects boundary edges (single-face adjacency) and non-manifold edges (three or more face adjacency).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_analysis.pv_extract_feature_edges")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_analysis.extract_feature_edges --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it feature_angle float 30.0 0.0 to 180.0 Dihedral angle threshold for feature edge detection (degrees). 30 degrees is VTK's default dihedral threshold: it catches machined edges and misses the facets of a smooth organ. boundary_edges string true Include boundary edges (true/false). true: open boundaries are what you look for on a scan with holes. non_manifold_edges string true Include non-manifold edges (true/false). true: non-manifold edges are the defects to fix before printing or simulation. manifold_edges string false Include regular manifold edges (true/false). false: regular edges would be every edge of the mesh. feature_edges (advanced) bool true Include feature (sharp dihedral-angle) edges. On: sharp edges are included. clear_data (advanced) bool false Drop point/cell data arrays from the output edges. Off: keep the scalar arrays on the edges.

docs.title: PyVista Mesh Processing
docs.text:
pyvista_mesh_processing: Mesh geometry operations powered by PyVista/VTK: decimation, subdivision, smoothing (Laplacian, Taubin), cleaning, hole filling, normal computation, triangulation, and surface extraction.

Methods pv_decimate, pv_subdivide, pv_smooth_laplacian, pv_smooth_taubin, pv_clean, pv_fill_holes, pv_compute_normals, pv_triangulate, pv_extract_surface Input files .ply, .obj, .stl, .vtk, .vtu Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_objaverse_glb_shard Example Label map to mesh on MSD hippocampus CLI pardesline run pyvista_mesh_processing.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
PyVista wraps VTK filters for mesh geometry processing. Operations include:

Decimation reduces triangle count using quadric error metrics. Subdivision refines meshes by splitting triangles (linear, butterfly, loop). Smoothing removes noise via Laplacian \(\mathbf{v}_i' = \mathbf{v}_i + \lambda \Delta \mathbf{v}_i\) or Taubin's \(\lambda|\mu\) scheme. Cleaning merges duplicate points and removes degenerate cells. Triangulation converts polygonal cells to triangles.

docs.title: pv_decimate
docs.text:
Reduces mesh complexity by collapsing edges based on quadric error metrics. Target reduction is a fraction \(r \in [0,1)\) of triangles to remove.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_decimate")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.decimate --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: MSD hippocampus surfaces (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh, decimate 0.5); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it target_reduction float 0.5 0.01 to 0.99 Fraction of triangles to remove (0.5 = remove 50%). 0.5 halves the triangle count: on marching-cubes output (one triangle per voxel face) that removes the redundant co-planar triangles with no visible change. volume_preservation (advanced) bool false Constrain decimation to preserve mesh volume (slower, less shrinkage). Off: VTK's default; on when the mesh is used for volume measurements (organs), since plain quadric decimation shrinks convex shapes slightly. attribute_error (advanced) bool false Include scalar/attribute error in the decimation cost metric. Off: ignore scalar fields in the error metric; on when a label or curvature field must survive decimation. normals (advanced) bool false Include normals deviation in the decimation cost metric. Off: do not penalise normal deviation; on for CAD meshes with sharp edges. boundary_constraints (advanced) bool false Use legacy boundary-edge-length weighting for boundary quadric constraints. Off: VTK's current boundary handling; the legacy weighting is for reproducing old results.

docs.title: pv_subdivide
docs.text:
Refines mesh by splitting triangles. Linear splits at midpoints; butterfly and loop use interpolation for smoother results.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_subdivide")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.subdivide --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it n_subdivisions int 1 1 to 4 Number of subdivision iterations. 1 iteration quadruples the triangle count, which is as much as a smoothing or sampling step ever needs. algorithm string linear Subdivision algorithm: linear, butterfly, or loop. linear keeps the surface exactly where it is and only adds vertices; butterfly and loop also smooth, which changes the geometry.

docs.title: pv_smooth_laplacian
docs.text:
Iteratively moves each vertex toward the centroid of its neighbors: \(\mathbf{v}_i' = \mathbf{v}_i + \lambda \frac{1}{|N_i|} \sum_{j \in N_i}(\mathbf{v}_j - \mathbf{v}_i)\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_smooth_laplacian")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.smooth_laplacian --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: MSD hippocampus surfaces (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it n_iterations int 20 1 to 500 Number of smoothing iterations. 20 iterations remove the voxel staircase of a marching-cubes surface; more than 50 visibly shrinks small structures. relaxation_factor float 0.01 0.001 to 1.0 Step size per iteration (higher = more smoothing). 0.01 is VTK's default step: small steps over 20 iterations move vertices by less than a voxel in total. convergence (advanced) float 0.0 0.0 to 1.0 Convergence threshold; smaller = more iterations. 0 disables early stop. 0 disables early stop so the iteration count is the only knob. edge_angle (advanced) float 15.0 0.0 to 180.0 Edge angle (deg) for interior edge features when feature_smoothing is on. 15 degrees is VTK's edge-feature threshold when feature smoothing is on. feature_angle (advanced) float 45.0 0.0 to 180.0 Feature angle (deg) for sharp-feature detection when feature_smoothing is on. 45 degrees is VTK's sharp-feature threshold when feature smoothing is on. boundary_smoothing (advanced) bool true Allow boundary (edge) vertices to move during smoothing. On: boundary vertices of open surfaces move too, otherwise the rim stays jagged. feature_smoothing (advanced) bool false Smooth along detected sharp features rather than freezing them. Off: organic surfaces have no sharp features to preserve; on for CAD parts.

docs.title: pv_smooth_taubin
docs.text:
Alternates shrinking (\(\lambda > 0\)) and inflating (\(\mu < 0\)) steps to smooth without volume shrinkage. Pass-band controls the cutoff frequency.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_smooth_taubin")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `mesh.smooth()`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.smooth_taubin --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: MSD hippocampus surfaces: the default mesh.smooth() (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it n_iterations int 20 1 to 500 Number of smoothing iterations. 20 iterations remove the voxel staircase; Taubin's pass band keeps the volume, so the count can be higher than for Laplacian smoothing without shrinkage. pass_band float 0.1 0.001 to 2.0 Pass-band value controlling cutoff frequency. 0.1 is VTK's default: frequencies above it are attenuated (staircase), below it kept (anatomy); lower it for a smoother result. edge_angle (advanced) float 15.0 0.0 to 180.0 Edge angle (deg) for interior edge features when feature_smoothing is on. 15 degrees, VTK's edge-feature threshold. feature_angle (advanced) float 45.0 0.0 to 180.0 Feature angle (deg) for sharp-feature detection when feature_smoothing is on. 45 degrees, VTK's sharp-feature threshold. boundary_smoothing (advanced) bool true Allow boundary (edge) vertices to move during smoothing. On so open rims are smoothed too. feature_smoothing (advanced) bool false Smooth along detected sharp features rather than freezing them. Off for organic surfaces. non_manifold_smoothing (advanced) bool false Also smooth non-manifold vertices. Off: non-manifold vertices (two sheets touching) are left in place to avoid tearing. normalize_coordinates (advanced) bool false Normalize coordinates before smoothing for better numerical stability. Off: VTK's default; on for coordinates with very large magnitudes (UTM metres) to keep the filter numerically stable.

docs.title: pv_clean
docs.text:
Merges coincident points, removes degenerate cells, and strips unused points within the specified tolerance.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_clean")  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `mesh.clean()`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.clean --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: every Mesh.clean() in the examples; generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it tolerance float 0.0 0.0 to 1.0 Merge tolerance (0 = exact duplicates only). 0 merges exact duplicates only: safe on any mesh; a positive tolerance welds nearby vertices and can close scan seams. point_merging (advanced) bool true Merge coincident points within tolerance. On: duplicate vertices from STL files and marching cubes are merged. absolute (advanced) bool true Interpret tolerance as an absolute distance (else fraction of bounding box). On: the tolerance is in file units, not a fraction of the bounding box, so it means the same thing on every mesh. lines_to_points (advanced) bool true Convert degenerate lines (zero length) to points. On: zero-length lines become points instead of invalid cells. polys_to_lines (advanced) bool true Convert degenerate polygons to lines. On: degenerate polygons become lines. strips_to_polys (advanced) bool true Convert degenerate triangle strips to polygons. On: degenerate strips become polygons.

docs.title: pv_fill_holes
docs.text:
Identifies boundary edges and fills holes smaller than the specified size by generating new triangular faces.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_fill_holes")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.fill_holes --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it hole_size float 100.0 1.0 to 10000.0 Maximum hole size to fill. 100 in file units is the largest hole (by boundary radius) that is filled: scan holes, not the open bottom of a bust.

docs.title: pv_compute_normals
docs.text:
Computes point and cell normals from triangle geometry. Consistency flips normals to face outward.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_compute_normals")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.compute_normals --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it flip_normals int 0 0 to 1 Flip all normals (0=no, 1=yes). 0: keep the file's orientation. consistency int 1 0 to 1 Enforce consistent normal orientation (0=no, 1=yes). 1: make neighbouring faces agree, which STL files from scanners often do not. cell_normals (advanced) bool true Compute per-cell (face) normals. On: per-face normals for rendering and sampling. point_normals (advanced) bool true Compute per-point (vertex) normals. On: per-vertex normals for smooth shading and registration. split_vertices (advanced) bool false Split vertices along sharp edges (creates duplicate points at hard edges). Off: splitting duplicates vertices along sharp edges and breaks the connectivity other steps rely on. auto_orient_normals (advanced) bool false Automatically orient normals outward (assumes a closed manifold). Off: it assumes a closed manifold and inverts open scans. non_manifold_traversal (advanced) bool true Prevent orientation propagation across non-manifold edges. On: orientation does not propagate across non-manifold edges, where it would flip. feature_angle (advanced) float 30.0 0.0 to 180.0 Feature angle (deg) used when split_vertices is on. 30 degrees when split_vertices is on, VTK's default.

docs.title: pv_triangulate
docs.text:
Converts all polygonal cells (quads, n-gons) into triangles for uniform processing.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_triangulate")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.triangulate --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: every Volume.to_mesh() surface is triangulated before saving (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated meshes in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

No tunable parameters.

docs.title: pv_extract_surface
docs.text:
Extracts the outer surface of a volumetric or unstructured grid as a polygonal mesh.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_extract_surface")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_mesh_processing.extract_surface --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: every Volume.to_mesh() result goes through surface extraction (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it pass_pointid (advanced) bool true Keep original point ids as a 'vtkOriginalPointIds' array on the surface. On: keep the original point ids so results can be mapped back to the volume. pass_cellid (advanced) bool true Keep original cell ids as a 'vtkOriginalCellIds' array on the surface. On: keep the original cell ids for the same reason. nonlinear_subdivision (advanced) int 1 0 to 4 Subdivision level for nonlinear (higher-order) cells; 1 matches the default. 1 matches VTK's default for higher-order cells; the grids here are linear.

docs.title: PyVista Point Cloud Processing
docs.text:
pyvista_pointcloud_processing: Point cloud and mesh filtering operations via PyVista: thresholding, clipping by plane/box, random sampling, and scalar-based point extraction.

Methods pv_threshold, pv_clip_plane, pv_clip_box, pv_random_sample, pv_extract_points Input files .ply, .pcd, .vtk, .vtu, .obj, .stl Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_objaverse_glb_shard CLI pardesline run pyvista_pointcloud_processing.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
PyVista provides spatial and scalar filtering for point data:

Threshold keeps points/cells within a scalar range. Clip removes geometry on one side of a plane. Clip Box crops to a bounding box. Random Sampling reduces data by random selection. Extract Points selects points matching scalar criteria.

docs.title: pv_threshold
docs.text:
Keeps cells whose scalar values satisfy \(l \leq s_i \leq u\) for lower bound \(l\) and upper bound \(u\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_pointcloud_processing.pv_threshold")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_pointcloud_processing.threshold --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it lower float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Lower scalar bound. 0 and upper 1 select a normalised scalar range; set them to your field's units (HU, reflectance). upper float 1.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Upper scalar bound. 1, see lower. scalars string "" Scalar array name (empty = active scalars). Empty uses the active scalar array, which is what a freshly loaded file has. invert (advanced) bool false Invert the threshold (keep values OUTSIDE the range). Off: keep what is inside the range. continuous (advanced) bool false Use continuous cell range: include cells whose scalar range overlaps [lower, upper]. Off: a cell is kept on its own scalar, not on the range it spans. preference (advanced) enum cell cell, point Whether to threshold on cell or point scalars when both exist. cell: VTK's default when both point and cell scalars exist. all_scalars (advanced) bool false Require all points of a cell to satisfy the criterion (else any point). Off: a cell is kept if any of its points pass, which keeps boundaries intact. component_mode (advanced) enum all all, any, component For multi-component scalars: test all components, any component, or a single one. all: every component of a vector scalar must pass. component (advanced) int 0 0 to 100 Component index to threshold when component_mode='component'. 0: the first component when component_mode is component.

docs.title: pv_clip_plane
docs.text:
Removes all geometry on the negative side of the plane \(\mathbf{n} \cdot (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{o}) = 0\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_pointcloud_processing.pv_clip_plane")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_pointcloud_processing.clip_plane --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it origin_x float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Plane origin X. 0: the plane passes through the origin by default; set it to a point on the cut you want. origin_y float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Plane origin Y. 0, see origin_x. origin_z float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Plane origin Z. 0, see origin_x. normal_x float 1.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Plane normal X. 1: cut perpendicular to x by default. normal_y float 0.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Plane normal Y. 0, see normal_x. normal_z float 0.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Plane normal Z. 0, see normal_x. invert (advanced) bool true Which side to keep. True (default) keeps the side the normal points away from. On keeps the side the normal points away from, VTK's convention for clip. value (advanced) float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Scalar offset of the clip plane along the normal. 0: no offset along the normal. crinkle (advanced) bool false Keep whole cells crossed by the plane instead of cutting them (crinkle clip). Off: cells crossed by the plane are cut, giving a flat face; on keeps them whole, which preserves the original cells.

docs.title: pv_clip_box
docs.text:
Keeps geometry inside the axis-aligned box \([x_{min}, x_{max}] \times [y_{min}, y_{max}] \times [z_{min}, z_{max}]\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_pointcloud_processing.pv_clip_box")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_pointcloud_processing.clip_box --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it x_min float -0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box X minimum. -0.5 to 0.5 is a unit box around the origin, the placeholder for normalised data; set the box in file units. x_max float 0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box X maximum. 0.5, see x_min. y_min float -0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box Y minimum. -0.5, see x_min. y_max float 0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box Y maximum. 0.5, see x_min. z_min float -0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box Z minimum. -0.5, see x_min. z_max float 0.5 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Box Z maximum. 0.5, see x_min. invert (advanced) bool false Invert the box selection (keep geometry OUTSIDE the box). Off: keep the inside of the box. merge_points (advanced) bool true Merge coincident points in the clipped output. On: coincident points created by the clip are merged. crinkle (advanced) bool false Keep whole cells crossed by the box instead of cutting them (crinkle clip). Off: cut the crossed cells.

docs.title: pv_random_sample
docs.text:
Uniformly samples a fraction \(f\) of the input points without replacement.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.ply")
result = obj.run("pyvista_pointcloud_processing.pv_random_sample")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_pointcloud_processing.random_sample --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it fraction float 0.5 0.01 to 1.0 Fraction of points to keep (0-1). 0.5 halves a cloud, the usual first step before an interactive look at a multi-million-point scan. replace (advanced) bool false Sample with replacement (allows duplicate picks). Off: no duplicate picks. seed (advanced) int -1 -1 to 2147483647 RNG seed for reproducibility; -1 = no seeding (non-deterministic, original behavior). -1 is non-deterministic, matching the original script; set a seed for reproducible figures. adjacent_cells (advanced) bool true Include cells that contain at least one selected point (else only fully-selected cells). On: cells touching a selected point are kept so meshes stay connected. include_cells (advanced) bool true Carry cells through to the output (else points only). On: carry cells through.

docs.title: pv_extract_points
docs.text:
Selects points whose scalar values lie within a specified range, producing a filtered point cloud.

result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Empty uses the active scalars. lower float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Lower bound for extraction. 0 with upper 1 is a normalised range placeholder. upper float 1.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Upper bound for extraction. 1, see lower. adjacent_cells (advanced) bool true Include cells that contain at least one selected point (else only fully-selected cells). On keeps connectivity. include_cells (advanced) bool true Carry cells through to the output (else points only). On carries cells through.

docs.title: PyVista Volume Processing
docs.text:
pyvista_volume_processing: Volumetric and grid processing via PyVista: isosurface extraction (contouring), slicing, thresholding, geometry extraction, and cell filtering.

Methods pv_contour, pv_slice, pv_slice_orthogonal, pv_threshold_volume, pv_extract_geometry, pv_extract_cells Input files .vti, .vtk, .vtu, .ply, .obj, .stl Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_objaverse_glb_shard CLI pardesline run pyvista_volume_processing.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
PyVista volume processing wraps VTK filters for extracting information from volumetric and grid datasets:

Contour/Isosurface extracts surfaces at scalar isovalues using marching cubes. Slice creates a cross-section along any plane. Threshold selects cells within a scalar range. Extract Geometry converts a volume to its surface representation. Extract Cells selects cells by type.

docs.title: pv_contour
docs.text:
Marching cubes extracts a surface mesh at scalar isovalue \(c\): \(\{\mathbf{x} : f(\mathbf{x}) = c\}\).

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.vti")
result = obj.run("pyvista_volume_processing.pv_contour")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_volume_processing.contour --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: MSD and RIRE volumes through Volume.to_mesh (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh, examples/spleen_ct_threshold_segmentation); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it n_contours int 5 1 to 50 Number of isosurface levels. 5 evenly spaced iso-levels show the structure of an unknown field; a label map or a known threshold uses one level through Volume.to_mesh. scalars string "" Scalar array name (empty = active scalars). Empty uses the active scalars (the image intensity). compute_normals (advanced) bool false Compute point normals on the output surface. Off: normals are recomputed later by the mesh steps that need them. compute_gradients (advanced) bool false Compute gradients at the isosurface. Off: not needed for a surface. compute_scalars (advanced) bool true Preserve the contoured scalar on the output. On: the contoured value is kept on the surface for colouring. method (advanced) enum contour contour, marching_cubes, flying_edges Contouring algorithm. contour is VTK's generic filter; marching_cubes and flying_edges are faster on image data and give the same surface. preference (advanced) enum point point, cell Prefer point or cell scalars. point: image intensities are point data.

docs.title: pv_slice
docs.text:
Intersects the dataset with a plane \(\mathbf{n} \cdot (\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{o}) = 0\) to produce a cross-section.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.vti")
result = obj.run("pyvista_volume_processing.pv_slice")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_volume_processing.slice --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: RIRE and MSD volumes (README demo slices); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it normal_x float 1.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Slice normal X. 1: an x-normal (sagittal in LPS) slice by default. normal_y float 0.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Slice normal Y. 0, see normal_x. normal_z float 0.0 -1.0 to 1.0 Slice normal Z. 0, see normal_x. origin_x float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Slice origin X (0 = center). 0 means the volume centre. origin_y float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Slice origin Y (0 = center). 0 means the centre. origin_z float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Slice origin Z (0 = center). 0 means the centre. generate_triangles (advanced) bool false Triangulate the slice output. Off: the slice stays a polygon mesh of quads. contour (advanced) bool false Generate contour edges of the slice. Off: no contour edges.

docs.title: pv_slice_orthogonal
docs.text:
Creates three orthogonal slices through the dataset at specified X, Y, Z positions.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.vti")
result = obj.run("pyvista_volume_processing.pv_slice_orthogonal")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_volume_processing.slice_orthogonal --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: MSD hippocampus MRI (examples/hippocampus_mask_to_mesh); generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it x float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 X position for YZ slice (0 = center). 0 means the centre of the volume. y float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Y position for XZ slice (0 = center). 0 means the centre. z float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Z position for XY slice (0 = center). 0 means the centre. generate_triangles (advanced) bool false Triangulate the slice output. Off: the slice stays a polygon mesh of quads, which renders and saves smaller. contour (advanced) bool false Generate contour edges of the slices. Off: no contour edges are generated on the slice.

docs.title: pv_threshold_volume
docs.text:
Selects cells with scalar values in \([l, u]\), preserving the volumetric structure.

import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("input.vti")
result = obj.run("pyvista_volume_processing.pv_threshold_volume")  # catalog defaults
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .vtu. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.pyvista_volume_processing.threshold_volume --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: generated grids in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it lower float 0.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Lower scalar bound. 0 with upper 1 is a normalised placeholder; use Hounsfield units on CT. upper float 1.0 -10000000000.0 to 10000000000.0 Upper scalar bound. 1, see lower. scalars (advanced) string "" Scalar array name (empty = active scalars). Empty uses the active scalars. invert (advanced) bool false Invert the threshold selection. Off: keep the inside of the range. continuous (advanced) bool false Use continuous cell range for thresholding. Off: a cell is kept on its own scalar value, not on the range it spans. preference (advanced) enum cell cell, point Prefer cell or point scalars. cell: VTK's default. all_scalars (advanced) bool false Require all scalar components to satisfy the range. Off: a cell is kept if any of its points pass, which keeps boundaries intact.

Extracts the boundary surface of a volume as a polygonal mesh.

docs.title: Point Cloud Registration
docs.text:
registration: Align point clouds into a common coordinate frame using RANSAC-based global registration and ICP local refinement.

Methods ransac_global, icp_refinement, ransac_icp_pipeline Input files .ply, .pcd, .txt, .xyz Two inputs input is the fixed reference, moving (Moving Cloud) is transformed Bundled datasets to try open3d_bunny, open3d_icp_demo, kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001, medshapenet, c3vd_endoscopy_splats Example RANSAC + ICP on the Stanford bunny CLI pardesline run registration.<method> input.ext [--param value]

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Point cloud registration finds the optimal rigid transformation \(T = (\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{t})\) that aligns a source point cloud \(P\) to a target \(Q\):

\[ T^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{t}} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \|\mathbf{R} p_i + \mathbf{t} - q_{c(i)}\|^2 \]

Global registration methods like RANSAC + FPFH features provide initial alignment before ICP refinement.

docs.title: ransac_global
docs.text:
RANSAC-based registration uses FPFH feature matching to establish correspondences, then estimates the best transformation from random subsets.

import pardesline as pl

fixed, moving = pl.load("fixed.ply"), pl.load("moving.ply")
result = fixed.run("registration.ransac_global", moving=moving)  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.ransac(moving=...)`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.registration.ransac_global --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny, 35 deg / 70 % overlap / 0.5 % noise (examples/icp_registration_bunny: 0.14 deg residual after ICP); ultrasound and CBCT reconstructions in the atlas-label-transfer skill (0.06 deg pose error on the bunny atlas); Open3D indoor fragments

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it voxel_size float 0.5 0 to 0.9 Voxel size for downsampling. 0 = auto-detect (1.3% of bbox diagonal, matches Open3D tutorial). 0.5 is a placeholder for the platform UI; 0 (auto) is what the one-call API passes: 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal, so the feature scale follows the object instead of a fixed number that is wrong for both a 15 cm part and a 15 m facade. normal_radius_factor (advanced) float 2.0 1.0 to 5.0 Normal-estimation radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 2x the voxel: normals need a neighbourhood a little larger than the downsampling cell to be stable but local. normal_max_nn (advanced) int 30 10 to 100 Max neighbors for normal estimation. 30 neighbours cap the normal estimation cost on dense clouds. fpfh_radius_factor (advanced) float 5.0 2.0 to 10.0 FPFH feature radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 5x the voxel is the Open3D-recommended FPFH support: large enough for a descriptive 33-bin histogram, small enough to stay local on partial scans. fpfh_max_nn (advanced) int 100 30 to 300 Max neighbors for the FPFH histogram. 100 neighbours bound the histogram cost. distance_threshold_factor (advanced) float 1.5 0.5 to 3.0 RANSAC max correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 1.5x the voxel: a correspondence within one and a half cells counts as an inlier; tighter rejects true matches on noisy scans, looser lets outliers vote. mutual_filter (advanced) bool true Use RANSAC mutual nearest-neighbor filtering. On: both directions of the feature match must agree, which removes most false correspondences before RANSAC and is the single setting that most improves success on symmetric parts. ransac_with_scaling (advanced) bool false Estimate a scale factor in the RANSAC transform. Off: rigid scans share a scale; turn on only for photogrammetry against a scanner. ransac_n (advanced) int 3 3 to 6 Correspondences sampled per RANSAC iteration. 3 correspondences is the minimum for a rigid transform; 4 helps on symmetric objects at the cost of more iterations. edge_length_threshold (advanced) float 0.9 0.0 to 1.0 Edge-length similarity threshold for RANSAC checker. 0.9: the pairwise distances of the sampled correspondences must agree within 10 %, which prunes wrong triplets before the expensive inlier count. ransac_max_iteration (advanced) int 100000 1000 to 4000000 Max RANSAC iterations. 100 000 iterations with the early-stop confidence below converge in seconds on 20k-point clouds. ransac_confidence (advanced) float 0.999 0.9 to 0.9999 RANSAC early-stop confidence. 0.999 stops once the best model is that likely to be the true one.

docs.title: icp_refinement
docs.text:
Iterative Closest Point alternates between finding correspondences via nearest-neighbor search and solving for \((\mathbf{R}, \mathbf{t})\) using SVD.

import pardesline as pl

fixed, moving = pl.load("fixed.ply"), pl.load("moving.ply")
result = fixed.run("registration.icp_refinement", moving=moving)  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `points.icp(moving=...)`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.registration.icp_refinement --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny (examples/icp_registration_bunny); Open3D indoor fragments; generated clouds in tests/test_ops_smoke.py

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it voxel_size float 0.5 0 to 0.9 Voxel size for downsampling. 0 = auto-detect (1.3% of bbox diagonal, matches Open3D tutorial). 0 (auto) picks 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal; the explicit 0.5 is the platform UI placeholder. max_iterations int 2000 100 to 10000 Maximum ICP iterations. 2 000 is a ceiling, not a target: point-to-plane ICP stops on the relative thresholds long before. icp_estimation_method (advanced) enum point_to_plane point_to_plane, point_to_point ICP estimation method (point-to-point remains the automatic fallback). point_to_plane converges in far fewer iterations and slides along surfaces instead of fighting them; point-to-point is the automatic fallback when normals cannot be estimated (sparse LiDAR). relative_fitness (advanced) float 1e-06 1e-08 to 0.001 ICP stop threshold on fitness change. 1e-6: stop when the inlier fraction no longer changes. relative_rmse (advanced) float 1e-06 1e-08 to 0.001 ICP stop threshold on RMSE change. 1e-6: stop when the inlier RMSE no longer changes. icp_threshold_factor (advanced) float 1.5 0.5 to 4.0 Downsampled-ICP correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 1.5x the voxel on the downsampled pass: generous so the first ICP pass can pull a coarse RANSAC pose in. refine_threshold_factor (advanced) float 0.4 0.2 to 2.0 Full-res refinement correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 0.4x the voxel on the full-resolution pass: tight so the last iterations are not pulled by points without a true counterpart (the 30 % non-overlap of a partial scan). normal_radius_factor (advanced) float 2.0 1.0 to 5.0 Normal-estimation radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 2x the voxel for normal estimation. normal_max_nn (advanced) int 30 10 to 100 Max neighbors for normal estimation. 30 neighbours cap the normal-estimation cost on dense clouds while keeping the covariance stable. fpfh_radius_factor (advanced) float 5.0 2.0 to 10.0 Pre-pass FPFH radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 5x the voxel for the RANSAC pre-pass features. fpfh_max_nn (advanced) int 100 30 to 300 Max neighbors for pre-pass FPFH. 100 neighbours bound the FPFH histogram cost; the radius, not the count, sets the feature scale. ransac_distance_factor (advanced) float 1.5 0.5 to 3.0 Pre-pass RANSAC correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 1.5x the voxel for the pre-pass inlier distance. mutual_filter (advanced) bool true Use RANSAC mutual filtering in the pre-pass. On for the pre-pass. ransac_with_scaling (advanced) bool false Estimate scale in the pre-pass RANSAC. Off: two rigid scans share a scale; estimating one only makes sense for photogrammetry against a scanner. ransac_n (advanced) int 3 3 to 6 Correspondences per pre-pass RANSAC iteration. 3 correspondences is the minimum that determines a rigid transform, which keeps the inlier probability per draw highest. edge_length_threshold (advanced) float 0.9 0.0 to 1.0 Edge-length similarity threshold (pre-pass). 0.9 edge-length agreement. ransac_max_iteration (advanced) int 100000 1000 to 4000000 Max pre-pass RANSAC iterations. 100 000 pre-pass iterations. ransac_confidence (advanced) float 0.999 0.9 to 0.9999 Pre-pass RANSAC confidence. 0.999 early stop. ransac_seed_fitness (advanced) float 0.3 0.0 to 1.0 Min RANSAC fitness to seed ICP (else center-of-mass init). 0.3: below this pre-pass fitness the features were not informative and ICP starts from the centre-of-mass alignment instead of a wrong pose.

docs.title: ransac_icp_pipeline
docs.text:
Complete pipeline: apply a known transformation, then recover it using RANSAC global alignment followed by ICP local refinement.

import pardesline as pl

fixed, moving = pl.load("fixed.ply"), pl.load("moving.ply")
result = fixed.run("registration.ransac_icp_pipeline", moving=moving)  # catalog defaults
# same thing, domain vocabulary: `target.align(moving)` on a `PointCloud`
result.provenance[-1]  # the step, every parameter used, duration, version

Output: .ply. Script: python -m pardesline.ops.registration.ransac_icp_pipeline --input ... --output ....

Defaults validated on: Stanford bunny, 35 deg / 70 % overlap / 0.5 % noise: 0.14 deg residual, inlier RMSE 0.9 mm against a 1.4 mm noise floor (examples/icp_registration_bunny); bunny atlas transfer 99.4 % label agreement (examples/atlas_label_transfer_bunny); Open3D indoor fragments

Parameter Type Default Range What it does Why this default, when to change it voxel_size float 0.5 0 to 0.9 Voxel size for downsampling. 0 = auto-detect (1.3% of bbox diagonal, matches Open3D tutorial). 0 (auto) = 1.3 % of the bounding-box diagonal: every other distance is a multiple of it, so one number adapts the whole pipeline to a 15 cm part or a 15 m facade; the explicit 0.5 is the platform UI placeholder. rotation_degrees float 45.0 5.0 to 90.0 Synthetic rotation for DEMO MODE only (when no moving cloud is connected). Ignored in real registration. 45 degrees is used only in demo mode (no moving cloud): a synthetic rotation large enough to defeat plain ICP so the global stage is visibly needed. normal_radius_factor (advanced) float 2.0 1.0 to 5.0 Normal-estimation radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 2x the voxel for stable but local normals. normal_max_nn (advanced) int 30 10 to 100 Max neighbors for normal estimation. 30 neighbours cap the normal-estimation cost on dense clouds while keeping the covariance stable. fpfh_radius_factor (advanced) float 5.0 2.0 to 10.0 FPFH feature radius as a multiple of voxel_size. 5x the voxel: the Open3D-recommended FPFH support. fpfh_max_nn (advanced) int 100 30 to 300 Max neighbors for the FPFH histogram. 100 neighbours bound the FPFH histogram cost; the radius, not the count, sets the feature scale. distance_threshold_factor (advanced) float 1.5 0.5 to 3.0 RANSAC max correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 1.5x the voxel for RANSAC inliers: tolerant to scanner noise, still rejects outliers. mutual_filter (advanced) bool true Use RANSAC mutual nearest-neighbor filtering. On: mutual nearest-neighbour matching is the setting that most reduces false correspondences on symmetric or repetitive parts. ransac_with_scaling (advanced) bool false Estimate a scale factor in the RANSAC transform. Off: two rigid scans share a scale; estimating one only makes sense for photogrammetry against a scanner. ransac_n (advanced) int 3 3 to 6 Correspondences sampled per RANSAC iteration. 3 correspondences, the minimum for a rigid transform. edge_length_threshold (advanced) float 0.9 0.0 to 1.0 Edge-length similarity threshold for RANSAC checker. 0.9: prune triplets whose pairwise distances disagree by more than 10 %. ransac_max_iteration (advanced) int 100000 1000 to 4000000 Max RANSAC iterations. 100 000 with early stop. ransac_confidence (advanced) float 0.999 0.9 to 0.9999 RANSAC early-stop confidence. 0.999 early-stop confidence. icp_threshold_factor (advanced) float 0.4 0.2 to 2.0 ICP correspondence distance as a multiple of voxel_size. 0.4x the voxel for the final ICP: tight, so the refinement is driven by true overlap and not by the partial-view points that have no counterpart. icp_estimation_method (advanced) enum point_to_plane point_to_plane, point_to_point ICP estimation method (point-to-point remains the automatic fallback). point_to_plane: faster convergence and no sliding across flat regions compared with point-to-point; point-to-point is the automatic fallback without normals. icp_max_iteration (advanced) int 30 1 to 2000 Max ICP iterations. 30 iterations after a good global pose is enough; the relative thresholds usually stop it earlier. icp_relative_fitness (advanced) float 1e-06 1e-08 to 0.001 ICP stop threshold on fitness change. 1e-6 stop on fitness plateau. icp_relative_rmse (advanced) float 1e-06 1e-08 to 0.001 ICP stop threshold on RMSE change. 1e-6 stop on RMSE plateau.
