docs.title: Point clouds, meshes, voxels and implicit fields: choosing a 3D representation
3D representations for deep learning
docs.text: "Your choice of 3D data structure shapes everything downstream: memory, model architecture, and what is even possible." The representation is a modelling decision, not a file format. pardesline keeps one Object per kind (PointCloud, Mesh, Volume/LabelMap, splat as a PointCloud with attributes) and converts between them only where the conversion is well posed.

docs.title: The four, side by side
docs.text:
Point cloud Mesh Voxel grid / SDF 3D Gaussian splat Stores unordered set vertices + faces (+ topology) regular grid of occupancy / density / signed distance set of anisotropic Gaussians: mean, covariance (scale + quaternion), opacity, SH colour Invariance to exploit permutation permutation of vertex order, but faces fix connectivity translation (convolution) none built in; differentiable rendering is the supervision Memory O(N), ~6 floats/point (xyz + normal) O(V + F), compact for surfaces O(n^3): a 512^3 float32 CT is 512 MB, 1 mm^3 over a torso ~59 floats/primitive (3 + 3 + 4 + 1 + 48 SH); 1-5 M primitives per scene Architectures PointNet / PointNet++ (set abstraction, FPS + ball query), DGCNN (edge conv on k-NN graph), Point Transformer v3, KPConv MeshCNN (edge-based), GNNs on the vertex graph, spectral CNNs, DiffusionNet 3D U-Net / nnU-Net, V-Net, MinkowskiNet and SpConv (sparse), octree CNNs (O-CNN), Swin-UNETR 3DGS rasteriser (tile-based, depth-sorted alpha blending), gsplat, feature splatting Strength sparse, native output of LiDAR / depth / scanners, no topology to maintain compact explicit surface, FEM-ready, exact normals and areas dense fields (CT, MRI, PET), convolutions, implicit surfaces at any iso-level photorealistic real-time novel views, differentiable w.r.t. images Weakness no surface, no neighbourhood structure without k-NN, density varies with distance hard to learn topology changes; needs clean (manifold) input cubic memory, aliasing of thin structures, resolution fixed heavy, needs posed images, geometry is implicit in opacities Where it is the native format LiDAR (KITTI, nuScenes), robotics, photogrammetry, intra-oral and surface scanners, ultrasound reconstructions CAD, graphics, biomechanics (heart / bone FEM), MedShapeNet, printed anatomy CT, MRI, PET, micro-CT, DBT, occupancy grids multi-view capture, endoscopy reconstruction (C3VD), KITTI-360 scene fits

Rule of thumb: learn on the representation your labels live in, convert only at the boundaries. Segmentation labels drawn on CT voxels train a voxel network; tooth labels painted on an intra-oral mesh train a mesh or point network; detection boxes from LiDAR train a point / pillar network.

docs.title: Memory and resolution arithmetic (do it before training)
docs.text:
• Voxel grids: n^3 * bytes. 256^3 float16 = 32 MB per channel; 3D U-Net activations at batch 2 with 32 base channels need ~10-16 GB. Patch-based training (128^3 or 96^3 crops, nnU-Net style) is the norm, never whole volumes. Isotropic resampling first: a 0.7 x 0.7 x 5 mm CT is not a cube.
  • Point clouds: PointNet++ with 4 096 input points, ball-query radii 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 in a unit sphere; a 3-M-point LiDAR chunk must be voxel-downsampled (point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample) or tiled first. Normalise to the unit sphere per sample and keep the scale factor to map predictions back.
  • Meshes: MeshCNN wants a fixed edge budget (e.g. 750-2 250 edges); decimate with pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_decimate (target_reduction) and keep it manifold (pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_clean). Faces are not a learnable quantity for most nets: they only define the graph.
  • Splats: 1 M Gaussians ~ 240 MB on disk as float32 PLY; training needs the rasteriser's per-tile sort each step (GPU only).

docs.title: Conversion matrix and the pardesline call for each arrow
docs.text:
From -> to Nature pardesline Notes mesh -> points exact sampling Mesh.to_points(num_points=) (mesh_processing.mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk) Poisson-disk gives even spacing; sample normals with the faces (use_triangle_normal) label map -> mesh exact (boundary of label k) LabelMap.to_mesh(label=k) marching cubes at 0.5 on the binary mask, direction cosines applied; result in LPS mm grey volume -> mesh parametric (iso-level) Volume.to_mesh(isovalue=v) choose v in the image units (HU for CT); never let code pick it points -> mesh lossy, parametric PointCloud.to_mesh() (point_cloud_reconstruction.poisson, depth, density_quantile) or point_cloud_reconstruction.ball_pivoting needs oriented normals; say "clean, density-trimmed surface", not watertight mesh -> voxels / SDF parametric voxel_to_mesh.voxelization (voxel_size), sdf.compute_sdf (voxel_size, level) voxel size sets the aliasing; SDF level 0 recovers the surface points -> voxels parametric voxel_to_mesh.voxelization after a surface, or an occupancy grid by binning binning loses sub-voxel detail; keep the spacing in the frame volume -> points parametric (spacing) LabelMap.to_mesh() then to_points() surface points only; for interior points, sample voxel centres with the affine points -> splat initialisation only gaussian-splatting skill, scripts/points_to_gaussians.py needs posed images to optimise; without them it is a visualisation splat -> points exact (means) read the PLY, keep x y z (and f_dc as colour) opacities below ~0.1 are usually floaters splat -> mesh best effort marching cubes on rendered depth / opacity fields (SuGaR, 2DGS) research-grade; validate against a scan

Each conversion in pardesline returns a new Object whose provenance keeps the method and parameters: a reviewer can see that a surface came from Poisson depth 9 with the 1 % lowest-density vertices removed.

docs.title: Pitfalls that break pipelines silently
docs.text:
1. Frames and units. DICOM/ITK volumes are LPS millimetres, NIfTI headers are RAS (ITK converts on load), glTF is Y-up metres, PLY/STL/OBJ carry nothing. A mesh from a CT (mm) overlaid on a LiDAR scan (m) is 1000x off. obj.frame.describe() says what is known; with_frame() declares, never guesses.
  2. Anisotropic voxels. Networks assume cubic voxels; resample to isotropic spacing (nnU-Net uses the median spacing of the dataset, or a fixed 1 x 1 x 1 mm) before cropping, and resample predictions back with nearest-neighbour for labels, linear for images.
  3. Label semantics. A label map is integers with a meaning table (LabelMap.labels). Resampling labels with linear interpolation invents intermediate classes; one-hot then argmax, or nearest-neighbour only.
  4. Point density bias. LiDAR density falls with distance; sampling 4 096 points uniformly over-represents near points. Voxel-downsample to a fixed spacing, then farthest-point-sample.
  5. Mesh topology. Poisson output has self-intersections where walls touch (nested heart chambers): reconstruct each structure separately.
  6. Orientation of normals. Poisson and ball pivoting fail on inconsistently oriented normals; features_extraction.normal_estimation with orient_k makes them consistent.
  7. Coordinates of a converted mesh. LabelMap.to_mesh applies spacing, origin and direction cosines; a hand-written marching cubes on GetArrayFromImage() (z, y, x order) does not. Compare bounding boxes.

docs.title: Choosing, by task (decision list)
docs.text:
• Organ / lesion segmentation on CT/MRI -> voxels (nnU-Net family), export surfaces afterwards with LabelMap.to_mesh.
  • Tooth / bone part segmentation on scanner meshes -> points (PointNet++ / Point Transformer) sampled from the mesh with labels transferred per face, or a mesh network when the connectivity carries the signal.
  • LiDAR detection -> points or pillars/voxels (PointPillars, CenterPoint), never meshes.
  • Registration -> points for rigid (RANSAC + ICP), voxels for multimodal intensity-based (Mattes MI), meshes for statistical shape models.
  • Shape statistics / biomechanics -> meshes with fixed correspondence.
  • Novel-view synthesis, telemedicine viewers, endoscopy replay -> splats.
  • Self-supervised pretraining on volumes (JEPA, MAE) -> voxel patches (3D ViT tokens of 16^3 or 8 x 16 x 16).

docs.title: Datasets to practise on (bundled)
docs.text:
open3d_bunny (mesh -> points -> Poisson -> SDF round trip), msd_task02_heart (label map -> left-atrium surface), totalsegmentator_ct (117 organ masks -> one mesh each), kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001 (LiDAR points, sensor frame), c3vd_endoscopy_splats (Gaussian splats + their centres), medshapenet (106 101 anatomical STL meshes).

import pardesline as pl

mask = pl.load("msd_task02_heart").filter(split="Tr")[0].mask  # LabelMap, LPS mm
surface = mask.to_mesh(label=1)  # exact boundary
points = surface.to_points(num_points=4096)  # for a point network
sdf = surface.run("sdf.compute_sdf", voxel_size=1.0)  # implicit field + marching cubes
surface.provenance[-1]["exact"], points.frame.describe()  # True, "LPS, mm (file)"

See references/conversion-matrix.md for the formulas behind each arrow.

docs.title: Atlas label transfer: labelling a scan from a labelled atlas
docs.text: Reference scripts: atlas_label_transfer.py.

docs.title: Atlas label transfer: from a labelled atlas to a segmented scan
docs.text:
The pipeline of PardesLine use case 01 (3-D ultrasound heart, 60 lines), made general and runnable locally with scripts/atlas_label_transfer.py.

atlas (points + per-point label)   scan (points, no labels, unknown pose)
          |                                   |
          +---- RANSAC + ICP (atlas -> scan) --+      registration.ransac_icp_pipeline
                         |
            aligned atlas, SAME point order  ->  labels still valid
                         |
          per-structure KD-tree distances; each scan point takes the closest structure
                         |
          per-label Poisson surface (density_quantile=0 -> closed) -> volume in mL
                         |
          evaluation: pose error, label agreement, per-structure Dice, volume vs atlas

docs.title: Step 1: registration (the scan is the fixed reference)
docs.text: The atlas moves onto the scan so that the scan's coordinates (and its frame, units, provenance) stay untouched. fixed.align(moving) keeps the moving cloud's point order in the output, so the atlas labels index the aligned points directly. Settings: voxel_size 2-5x the point spacing (auto when the units are right), point-to-plane ICP, ransac_with_scaling=False unless the atlas is in different units (then fix the units instead). See point-cloud-registration for every parameter and failure mode. Expect fitness 0.6-0.95 on partial, noisy ultrasound; inlier RMSE near the noise floor (0.5-1 mm).

docs.title: Step 2: nearest-structure label transfer
docs.text:
For each structure k, compute the distance from every scan point to the aligned atlas points of structure k (one KD-tree per structure); assign argmin_k. This differs from "label of the single nearest atlas point": per-structure minima are robust to a few mislabelled atlas points and to density differences. Reject scan points whose minimum distance exceeds a tolerance (2-3x the noise, or the atlas point spacing) as unlabelled rather than forcing a label; report their fraction.

Refinements when needed: majority vote in a k-neighbourhood of the scan (smooths salt-and-pepper labels at boundaries); a non-rigid CPD step (deformable_registration.cpd_deformable) after the rigid alignment when the patient's anatomy differs in shape, with the folding check from evaluation-metrics-3d.

docs.title: Step 3: surfaces and volumes
docs.text: Poisson reconstruction expects one closed surface: reconstruct each structure separately (PointCloud.to_mesh(depth=8, density_quantile=0.0, normal_radius=...)), never the nested chambers together (that produces a tangle). density_quantile=0 keeps every vertex so the mesh stays closed and its volume is meaningful; normal_radius must be in the data's units (mm: 3-6; the catalog default 0.1 is for metre-scale scenes). Volume = PyVista mass_properties on a mesh with n_open_edges == 0; mm^3 / 1000 = mL.

docs.title: Step 4: evaluation (what to report)
docs.text:
Quantity How Meaning Pose error rotation (deg) and translation at the object centre against the true transform (synthetic or phantom) the registration itself Label agreement fraction of scan points whose transferred label equals the label obtained with the true transform the transfer, independent of the registration quality Per-structure surface Dice / HD95 between transferred and reference structures where it fails (small chambers) Volume per structure, vs the atlas or a reference measurement the clinically read number Unlabelled fraction points beyond the tolerance honesty about partial scans

"100 % label accuracy" on a scan generated from the atlas itself is a pipeline sanity check; on a real patient, expect 85-95 % at chamber boundaries and report where the 5-15 % sits.

docs.title: Building an atlas with pardesline
docs.text:
A labelled atlas is a point cloud with a label per point. From a label map:

import pardesline as pl, numpy as np

s = pl.load("totalsegmentator_ct")[0]  # 117 organ masks
atlas_points, atlas_labels = [], []
for k, organ in enumerate(["heart", "aorta", "lung_upper_lobe_left", "lung_upper_lobe_right"], start=1):
    pts = s.get(organ).to_mesh(label=1).to_points(num_points=4000).to_numpy()  # LPS mm
    atlas_points.append(pts)
    atlas_labels.append(np.full(len(pts), k))
atlas = np.vstack(atlas_points)
labels = np.concatenate(atlas_labels)

Or from msd_task02_heart (left atrium), amos22 (15 organs), MedShapeNet STL meshes (medshapenet, one structure per file). Keep the atlas frame and units with the arrays (write a .pardesline.json sidecar or a manifest role with labels).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Units: an atlas in mm and a scan in m never register (fitness ~0). Check frame.describe() on both.
  • Point order: any operation that reorders the aligned atlas (voxel downsampling, outlier removal) breaks the label mapping; transfer labels from the aligned output of the registration, which keeps the order, or carry labels as a colour attribute.
  • Partial scans: fitness caps at the overlap; the unlabelled fraction tells the truth.
  • Symmetric structures (two ventricles, paired kidneys) can swap: verify with a landmark or the volume ordering.
  • Noise: outlier removal on the scan before registration (point_cloud_processing.statistical_outlier_removal) improves both stages.

docs.title: Datasets to practise on
docs.text:
open3d_bunny (synthetic atlas, the script), medshapenet (pairs of the same organ from different patients, ds.filter(structure="liver")), totalsegmentator_ct / amos22 (build atlases), c3vd_endoscopy_splats (points role: scene-to-scene transfer).

Source: skills/atlas-label-transfer/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: pl.run
docs.text:
res = pl.run("simpleitk_registration", "rigid", "ct.mha", moving="mr.mha", num_iterations=200)
res = pl.run("point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample", "scan.ply", "small.ply", voxel_size=0.02)
res.output      # Path written (default: pl.output_dir()/<stem>_<method>_<id>.<ext>)
res.sidecar     # Path of <output>.json when the script wrote one (registration), else None
res.log         # full stdout+stderr of the script, ANSI stripped
res.duration_s, res.command, res.params (as sent), res.provenance()

Signature: run(module, method=None, input=None, /, output=None, *, moving=None, params=None, timeout=600, python=None, on_log=None, on_progress=None, cwd=None, **params). The first three are positional-only, so a parameter literally called method or input (e.g. pv_contour(method="flying_edges")) still works as a keyword. params={...} and keywords may be mixed but not repeat.

Validation before execution (raises pl.ParameterError): unknown name (with a "did you mean"), wrong type, out of [min..max], enum not in options (case-insensitive, normalised), output extension not the method's, input extension not accepted by the module, moving missing for a two-input method or given to a single-input one. Coercion to the command line: floats repr, bools true/false, lists joined with commas (shrink_factors=[4, 2, 1]).

Execution: a subprocess python -m pardesline.ops.<module>.<script> --input ... --output ... [--moving ...] --name value ... with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1, MPLBACKEND=Agg, PYVISTA_OFF_SCREEN=true, LOGURU_COLORIZE=False. Lines starting with PROGRESS:NN go to on_progress(int); every other line goes to on_log(str) or to loguru at DEBUG. timeout kills the child and raises pl.RunError (.returncode is None); a non-zero exit raises pl.RunError with the last 25 log lines in str(err); exit 0 without an output file is also a RunError.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
pardesline list [--ext .mha] [--category registration]
pardesline describe simpleitk_registration.rigid
pardesline run point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample scan.ply -o small.ply --voxel_size 0.02
pardesline run simpleitk_registration.rigid ct.mha --moving mr.mha -o reg.vti --num_iterations 200 -q
pardesline version

Parameters after the input are --name value (booleans --flag true). The run prints the output path (and the sidecar path) on stdout and echoes the script log on stderr unless -q. Exit code 1 with error: ... on any PardesLineError or missing file. The cloud commands (login, upload, send, inbox, ls, download, share, whoami, logout) are forwarded to the cloud client.

docs.title: Running a script directly (same contract as the hosted platform)
docs.text:
python -m pardesline.ops.simpleitk_segmentation.otsu_threshold --input ct.mha --output mask.vti
python -m pardesline.ops.registration.icp_refinement --input fixed.ply --output moved.ply --moving moving.ply --voxel_size 0.05

Exit 0 means the output was written. Prefer pl.run from Python: it validates, names the output and captures the log.

Source: skills/catalog-and-run/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
src/pardesline/
  _version.py            single version source (hatchling reads it)
  __init__.py            public API; cloud helpers and pl.o3d/pv/sitk/np resolved lazily
  errors.py              PardesLineError (shared with cloud) + Catalog/Parameter/Run/Manifest/Fetch/NeedsConfirmation
  catalog/               Catalog, Module, Method, Parameter + data/<module>.json (19 files, the 73 methods)
  runner.py              pl.run: validation, subprocess, log/progress capture, RunResult
  object/                Object classes, frame.py (Frame, License, format defaults), convert.py (in-process conversions)
  data/                  manifest.py (pydantic schema incl. Layout), dataset.py (+ export), scan.py (folders and listings), cache.py, sources/{local,https,hf,archive,s3,tcia,urllist,open3d}.py, manifests/*.json
  object/arrays.py       raw .npy/.npz/.bin decoding through a layout; pure-NumPy PLY writer; grid -> MetaImage
  ops/<module>/*.py      the 73 scripts, byte-identical to the hosted platform's modules/*/scripts
  medical/               _service.py + pyvista_adapter.py (the platform's SimpleITK service), public re-exports
  cloud/                 the 0.1.0 cloud client, verbatim
tests/                   fast tests + ops smoke tests + 73 --help checks + network tests
skills/                  these skills (installable as a Claude Code plugin)

The hosted platform's modules/ folder and services are the source of truth for ops/, catalog/data/ and medical/ until the platform depends on this package; those files are excluded from ruff and must stay byte-identical (only the ten SimpleITK scripts have their import rewired to pardesline.medical._service). Edit algorithms upstream, or deliberately fork here and document it in CHANGELOG.

docs.title: Adding an algorithm
docs.text:
1. src/pardesline/ops/<module>/<name>.py: argparse with --input, --output, optional --moving, typed flags for every parameter (_b helper for booleans accepting true/false), loguru logging, sys.exit(1) on failure, if __name__ == "__main__": main(). Lists arrive as "4,2,1" strings, enums as their option text, booleans as true/false. Print PROGRESS:NN for long runs. Write the output at --output exactly; a registration op writes <output>.json beside it.
  2. Catalog entry in src/pardesline/catalog/data/<module>.json: {"id", "name", "script", "output_extension", "dual_input"?, "parameters": [ {"name", "type": float|int|bool|enum|string|list, "default", "description", "min"?, "max"?, "options"? (enum), "advanced"?}]}. Parameter names must not be output, moving, params, timeout, python, on_log, on_progress, cwd. Every parameter needs a description and a default that passes its own range; tests/test_catalog.py checks that each --name exists in the script (shared registration flags may live in medical/_service.py).
  3. A smoke test in tests/test_ops_smoke.py on generated data, marked local or medical. tests/test_scripts_help.py will run --help on it.
  4. Update the module table in README.md and the catalog-and-run skill.

docs.title: Adding a bundled dataset
docs.text:
1. src/pardesline/data/manifests/<name>.json: explicit samples for a small https / open3d excerpt, or a pattern per role for a hub repo or a remote archive; license (SPDX id, commercial, source_url, note ending in TO CONFIRM when the terms were not established), citation, size_mb, tags. Names: hf_* for Hub repos, otherwise the dataset's usual short name.
  2. https files need the SHA-512 (or the upstream md5) of the download; archives need archive: true and the member path as the key. hf sources must scope the listing with paths (a whole 100k-file repo is rate-limited before it is listed); check the real tree with HfApi().list_repo_tree(repo, path_in_repo=..., repo_type="dataset"). archive sources need a url (or urls) whose server honours Range requests (probe with a Range: bytes=0-0 GET -> 206); s3 sources a bucket that allows anonymous ListObjectsV2; tcia sources the exact NBIA collection name (getCollectionValues). Any .npy/.npz/.bin role needs its layout; verify it on one real file. Record in the description what was measured (index size, fetch time).
  3. tests/test_manifest.py validates every bundled manifest offline (patterns, layouts, licence id, paths for hf); add a network test in tests/test_network.py (PARDESLINE_NETWORK_TESTS=1) that lists the dataset and fetches its smallest member.
  4. Mention it in README (Datasets), CHANGELOG and the datasets skill.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
pytest -q -m "not slow"                      # ~1 min: catalog, params, runner, object, manifests, scan, https (local server), cloud unit
pytest -q                                    # + ops smoke (real Open3D/PyVista/SimpleITK runs) + 73 --help checks (~6 min)
PARDESLINE_NETWORK_TESTS=1 pytest tests/test_network.py   # real downloads (RIRE 19 MB, liver, Open3D bunny)
ruff check . && ruff format --check .

Markers: local (skips without Open3D+PyVista), medical (without SimpleITK), slow, network. The conftest.py fixture out_dir routes pl.output_dir() into the test's temp folder. The https source is tested against a ThreadingHTTPServer in-process (hash mismatch, mirrors, archives, cache reuse).

docs.title: CI and release
docs.text: .github/workflows/ci.yml: lint; core tests on 3.10 and 3.13 without native libs (-m "not local and not medical"); full tests on Ubuntu / Windows / macOS with 3.10 and 3.12 (apt installs libgl1, libegl1, libusb-1.0-0 for Open3D); build + twine check. publish.yml uses PyPI Trusted Publishing on a GitHub release (environment pypi, no token). Bump _version.py and CHANGELOG, tag vX.Y.Z, create the release.

docs.title: Gotchas already paid for
docs.text:
• hatchling honours .gitignore: a data/ pattern once dropped catalog/data/*.json from the wheel. Use anchored patterns (/data/). Always inspect the wheel (zipfile) before a release.
  • A catalog parameter is named method (pv_contour): pl.run and Object.run take module, method, input positional-only.
  • [medical] needs PyVista: SimpleITK cannot read .vti, every SimpleITK op writes .vti.
  • Child processes: set LOGURU_COLORIZE=False and strip ANSI; keep user-facing strings ASCII (em-dashes and ellipses turn into ? on Windows pipes).
  • Open3D 0.19 has no Python 3.13 wheels; pin open3d>=0.18,<0.20 (0.20 broke headless Linux: libEGL/libusb).
  • .txt is an accepted point-cloud extension for ops but too ambiguous for pl.scan, which skips it.

Source: skills/contributing-algorithms/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Datasets and manifests
docs.text: pl.load never knows a dataset; it knows a manifest. A manifest says where the files come from (with checksums or a hub revision), under which terms, how files group into samples, and what the files cannot say by themselves (frame, units, label meanings, the layout of a raw array). Same code path for a bundled public dataset, a Hugging Face repo, a remote archive and a private folder.

sweep.frame.describe()  # "sensor, m (manifest)"
objects = sweep.run("ground_removal").run("object_clustering", eps=0.7, min_points=10)

docs.title: Any public bucket or TCIA collection: s3://, tcia://
docs.text: pl.load("s3://openneuro.org/ds000001") lists the prefix of a public bucket (ListObjectsV2, anonymous, paginated, cached, capped at 20 000 keys) and drafts a manifest; OpenNeuro's licence (CC0 / PDDL) is filled in. When nothing is left to ask (NIfTI carries its frame) the dataset loads directly. pl.load("tcia://Pancreas-CT/CT") lists the series of a public TCIA collection through the NBIA API (one entry per series, named <PatientID>/<Modality>/<SeriesInstanceUID>/; the optional /CT,MR part filters modalities); each series downloads as a zip of DICOM files on first access and becomes a DICOM Volume. Restricted collections answer 401 and are left to the NBIA Data Retriever. A manifest routes modalities to roles with patterns such as {id}/CT/{series} (id = patient) and {id}/SEG/{series}.

docs.title: Any Hugging Face repo: hf://org/name[/sub/folder]
docs.text:
• With a bundled manifest for that repo: loads it. A sub-folder re-scopes the listing: pl.load("hf://MIC-DKFZ/OpenMind/OpenMind/ds000003").
  • Without one: the package lists the folder, drafts a manifest and asks exactly as for a private folder (pl.NeedsConfirmation): the licence (taken from the Hub card when it states one, still marked TO CONFIRM), units and frame of formats that carry none, label meanings, and the layout + types of raw arrays. Answer in the call, edit the draft saved under pl.cache_dir()/drafts/, interactive=True, or assume=True.
  • pl.scan("hf://org/name/sub") returns the draft without raising.
  • Listing is per sub-folder (list_repo_tree), cached on disk for the repo commit, capped by source.max_files (20 000): a 266 721-file repo such as OpenMind is never listed whole (that takes 15 minutes and ends in HTTP 429 for anonymous clients). Tell the user to set HF_TOKEN or run huggingface-cli login for higher limits and for gated repos; the package never scripts past a click-through.
pl.load("hf://acme/scans/raw")
# NeedsConfirmation: hf_acme_scans: 3 question(s) ...
#   - roles.scan.layout: raw/p01/scan.bin is a raw array. What is in it? ...
ds = pl.load(
    "hf://acme/scans/raw",
    types={"scan": "points"},
    layout={"scan": {"dtype": "float32", "shape": "(N,4)", "columns": ["x", "y", "z", "i"]}},
    units={"scan": "m"},
    frame={"scan": "sensor"},
)

docs.title: Dataset API
docs.text:
• Indexing: ds[i], ds["sample_id"], iteration, len, ds.ids.
  • Subsets (lazy, same source): ds.take(n), ds.sample(n, seed=0), ds.filter(split="Tr") on sample fields (pattern placeholders become fields).
  • ds.split(by=None, fractions=(0.8, 0.2), seed=0) -> tuple of Datasets; every sample sharing the by field (default the manifest pairing key) lands in one part.
  • By role or type: ds.role("ct"), ds.volumes, ds.meshes, ds.points (iterators), ds.roles, ds.manifest, ds.license, ds.citation.
  • ds.fetch_all() downloads everything now. ds.export(folder) writes a standard copy: raw arrays become PLY / MetaImage through their layout, DICOM series one .mha, every file with its .pardesline.json sidecar, plus a local pardesline.manifest.json so pl.load(folder) reopens it without questions. CLI: pardesline export msd_task02_heart ./heart --take 2.
  • Sample: s.get("ct"), s["ct"], s.ct (cached), s.path("ct") (local path after fetch), s.id, s.fields, s.license, s.describe().

Objects from a dataset carry role, the dataset licence, the role's frame (source="manifest", never overriding a header), labels, layout, meta["modality"], and a first provenance step {"step": "load", "dataset", "sample", "role", "source"}.

docs.title: The manifest schema (pydantic, extra="forbid")
docs.text:
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "name": "study_a",                       // ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*$
  "title": "...", "description": "...",
  "source": {"scheme": "local", "root": "/data/study_a"},
  "license": {"spdx": "CC-BY-4.0", "commercial": true, "source_url": "...", "note": "...",
              "requires_agreement": false, "redistribution": "allowed|forbidden|unknown"},
  "citation": "...", "homepage": "...",
  "pairing": "patient",                     // the field that groups samples for split()
  "roles": {
    "ct":   {"type": "volume", "pattern": "{id}/ct/*.dcm", "frame": "LPS", "units": "mm", "modality": "CT"},
    "mask": {"type": "labels", "pattern": "{id}/seg.nii.gz", "labels": {"1": "left_atrium"}},
    "mesh": {"type": "mesh",   "pattern": "{id}/la.stl", "units": "mm", "frame": "LPS"},
    "lidar": {"type": "points", "pattern": "{id}.bin", "frame": "sensor", "units": "m",
              "layout": {"dtype": "float32", "shape": "(N,4)", "columns": ["x","y","z","reflectance"]}},
    "occ":  {"type": "labels", "pattern": "{id}.npz",
              "layout": {"key": "occ_label", "shape": "(200,200,16)", "spacing": [0.4,0.4,0.4]}}
  },
  "samples": [ {"id": "p01", "files": {"ct": "p01/ct", "mask": "p01/seg.nii.gz"}, "fields": {"patient": "p01"}} ],
  "size_mb": 120, "tags": ["medical"],
  "questions": []                           // non-empty = draft (see scanning-private-folders)
}

Role types: volume, labels, mesh, points, image, transform, splat, attribute, calibration, file. Either list samples explicitly (small bundled datasets and gated repos do) or give every role a pattern: {id} names the sample; other placeholders ({study}/{subject}, images{split}/{id}) become sample fields and, without {id}, join into the sample id (ds000001/sub-01); a repeated placeholder ({id}/anat/{id}_T1w.nii.gz) must match the same text; * matches within a path segment, ** across. Several DICOM files for one role collapse to their folder (fetched whole on access); a folder entry from a listing (.../series/) is a DICOM series; a second non-DICOM match is reported and the first kept. A .mhd header brings its .raw / .zraw sibling along.

Raw arrays need a layout. A role whose files are .npy, .npz, .bin or .raw must carry layout: shape ("(N,4)" for points, "(L,W,H)" for a grid), columns naming x, y, z and the attributes, dtype (required for headerless .bin), key for an .npz, optional spacing / origin for grids and scale for colours. The manifest validator refuses a non-draft manifest without it; the package never guesses a layout.

Sources:

scheme fields behaviour local root (absolute, or relative to the manifest file) files on disk https files: {relpath: {sha512 or md5, url?, archive?, archive_root?, size_mb?}}, mirrors? download from url then hash-addressed mirrors, verify, cache under ~/.cache/pardesline/datasets/<name>/; archive: true = the download is a tar/zip whose members land in the file's folder (or archive_root) hf repo_id, revision="main", repo_type="dataset", paths (sub-folders to list), max_files=20000 huggingface_hub listing per folder (cached per commit) and per-file download; the user's own token for gated repos archive url or urls (several archives forming one dataset), format zip/tar (inferred), prefix, optional sha512/md5 (single url) remote archives read by HTTP Range: index (zip central directory, incl. zip64; tar headers) cached on disk, each member fetched alone and CRC-checked (zip); whole download once when the server ignores ranges; compressed tars not supported; fetch_folder for DICOM series inside s3 bucket, endpoint (default AWS), prefix, max_files public bucket listing (ListObjectsV2) and plain HTTPS downloads; relative paths are the keys under prefix tcia collection, modalities?, api NBIA REST API: getSeries listing cached on disk, getImage zip per series unpacked into a folder urllist index_url, strip_prefix?, max_files a text file with one URL per line (MedShapeNet); relative path = file name open3d dataset (class name in open3d.data) Open3D downloads its own demo data

Licence tiers for public data: permissive (CC-BY, MIT, ODC-By) may be mirrored; non-commercial (KITTI, KiTS23) loader only with commercial: false; gated / DUA (ShapeNet, BraTS, TCIA restricted) requires_agreement: true, user credentials. Never redistribute; put the upstream terms in note and mark TO CONFIRM when not established.

docs.title: Writing and loading your own manifest
docs.text:
Manifest.from_dict(...), Manifest.load(path), m.save(path), m.describe(), m.to_json(). pl.load("study.manifest.json") opens it (relative local roots resolve against the file); pl.load("hf://org/name", manifest="my.json") binds one to a repo. Validation errors raise pl.ManifestError with the field path. Cache: pl.cache_dir(), pl.set_cache_dir(path), env PARDESLINE_CACHE; huggingface_hub keeps its own cache (HF_HOME).

Source: skills/datasets-and-manifests/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: 3D Gaussian splatting for point-cloud and medical engineers
docs.text: Reference scripts: points_to_gaussians.py.

docs.title: What a primitive is
docs.text:
A scene is a set of N anisotropic 3D Gaussians G_i(x) = exp(-1/2 (x - mu_i)^T Sigma_i^-1 (x - mu_i)), each with

Attribute Parameters Stored as position mu 3 x y z covariance Sigma = R S S^T R^T 3 log-scales + 4 quaternion scale_0..2 (log), rot_0..3 (w x y z, unnormalised) opacity alpha = sigmoid(o) 1 opacity (logit) colour, spherical harmonics degree 3 3 + 45 f_dc_0..2, f_rest_0..44

59 floats, versus 6 for a point with a normal. The factorisation R S S^T R^T keeps Sigma positive semi-definite under gradient descent: R comes from a normalised quaternion and S from exponentiated scales.

docs.title: Point cloud -> splats: the five-step initialisation
docs.text:
1. mu_i = p_i (keep the cloud's frame and units; splats have no unit either).
  2. s_i = log(mean distance to the k = 3 nearest neighbours) on all three axes: dense regions get small Gaussians, sparse ones large; an isotropic start that the optimiser can stretch.
  3. q_i = (1, 0, 0, 0) identity rotation.
  4. o_i = logit(0.1) so every primitive starts faint and the optimiser can raise the useful ones.
  5. f_dc = (rgb - 0.5) / C_0, C_0 = 0.28209479 (the degree-0 SH basis constant); f_rest = 0 (view-independent start).

scripts/points_to_gaussians.py does exactly this with NumPy and writes the PLY that gsplat, the reference implementation and web viewers read. Without images to optimise against the result is a visualisation of the cloud (it fills gaps and renders fast); with posed images it is the standard initialisation (the original method starts from a COLMAP SfM cloud).

docs.title: Rendering (why it is real time)
docs.text: Project each Gaussian to the image plane with the camera Jacobian J: Sigma' = J W Sigma W^T J^T (a 2D Gaussian). Tile the screen (16 x 16), sort the Gaussians touching each tile by depth (one radix sort per frame), then alpha-blend front to back: C = sum_i c_i alpha_i prod_{j<i} (1 - alpha_j). Every step is differentiable w.r.t. all attributes, so the photometric loss trains geometry and appearance together. 30+ fps at 1080p on a consumer GPU for 1-3 M primitives; NeRF needs seconds per frame.

docs.title: Training (the reference recipe, Kerbl et al. 2023)
docs.text:
• Loss: (1 - lambda) L1 + lambda (1 - SSIM), lambda = 0.2.
  • Adam with per-attribute learning rates: position 1.6e-4 (scaled by scene extent, decayed to 1.6e-6), SH 2.5e-3 (f_rest at 1/20), opacity 0.05, scale 5e-3, rotation 1e-3.
  • Adaptive density control every 100 iterations from 500 to 15 000: clone small Gaussians with large positional gradient (> 2e-4) in under-reconstructed areas, split large ones (scale > 1 % of extent) in over-reconstructed areas, prune opacity < 0.005 and oversized Gaussians; reset opacities every 3 000 iterations to kill floaters.
  • 30 000 iterations; SH degree raised by one every 1 000 iterations.
  • Evaluate on held-out views: PSNR (> 25 dB good indoors), SSIM, LPIPS (lower is better). Report memory (primitives, MB) and fps.

Libraries: gsplat (Nerfstudio, CUDA, pip), the original graphdeco-inria/gaussian-splatting, nerfstudio (splatfacto), web viewers (antimatter15/splat, gsplat.js on the Hub). Variants: 2DGS (surfels, better geometry), SuGaR (mesh extraction), Mip-Splatting (aliasing), 4DGS / Deformable-GS (dynamic scenes, surgery).

docs.title: Medical and endoscopy
docs.text:
• Endoscopy / laparoscopy: EndoGaussian, EndoGSLAM, PR-ENDO on EndoNeRF, SCARED and C3VD. Tissue deforms: dynamic variants add a deformation field mu_i(t); depth supervision (stereo or monocular prior) stabilises the geometry where texture is poor.
  • CT/MRI are volumes, not photographs: splats are not a segmentation or a volume representation; use them for rendering a surface extracted from a volume (initialise from LabelMap.to_mesh().to_points()), for surgical video replay, or for digital twins of a room/instrument.
  • Telemedicine viewers: a splat of a dental arch or a wound renders on a phone; a mesh with textures is usually enough and lighter to validate.

docs.title: Reading, writing, converting
docs.text:
• A splat PLY is a vertex-only PLY with the fields above; pl.load opens it as a PointCloud (the means), Open3D keeps x y z and ignores the rest. c3vd_endoscopy_splats ships ten such files (splat role) and their means (points role); hf_3d_arena has the SAM-3D-Objects-3DGS outputs; the KITTI-360 subset stores the attributes as separate .npy arrays (hf_kitti360_gs_subset, roles gaussian_centers, gaussian_scale, ...).
  • Splat -> points: keep means with sigmoid(opacity) > 0.1.
  • Splat -> mesh: SuGaR / 2DGS extract a surface; validate against a scan or a label-map mesh (evaluation-metrics-3d).
  • Other formats: .splat (antimatter15: 32 bytes per Gaussian, SH degree 0), .spz (Niantic, compressed), glTF KHR_gaussian_splatting (draft).
import pardesline as pl

cloud = pl.load("open3d_bunny")[0].mesh.to_points(num_points=50000)
# scripts/points_to_gaussians.py cloud.path out.ply --colour 0.8 0.7 0.6

docs.title: Trade-offs to state
docs.text:
Splats buy photorealism and speed with memory (10-50x a mesh of the same surface), a per-frame sort, no explicit surface (normals, areas and volumes need extraction), and a dependence on good camera poses. For measurement, simulation or printing, convert to a mesh and validate it.

Source: skills/gaussian-splatting/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Mcp server
docs.text: title: "The MCP server" description: "Run and use pardesline as a local MCP server (pardesline mcp, pip install "pardesline[mcp]"): the stdio / streamable-http transports, the configuration"

docs.title: The pardesline MCP server
docs.text:
pip install "pardesline[mcp]"        # or [all]
pardesline mcp                        # stdio: what every MCP client spawns
pardesline mcp --transport streamable-http --port 8765   # http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp

Everything runs on the user's machine, without a PardesLine account. The only network traffic is the downloads the user asks for (one sample at a time). Logs go to stderr (PARDESLINE_LOG=DEBUG); stdout is the protocol channel.

docs.title: Connecting a client
docs.text:
Client Configuration Claude Code claude mcp add pardesline -- pardesline mcp (or the repo's .mcp.json; the plugin declares the server too) Claude Desktop claude_desktop_config.json: "mcpServers": {"pardesline": {"command": "pardesline", "args": ["mcp"]}} Cursor .cursor/mcp.json: same mcpServers block Gemini CLI ~/.gemini/settings.json: "mcpServers": {"pardesline": {"command": "pardesline", "args": ["mcp"]}} Codex CLI ~/.codex/config.toml: [mcp_servers.pardesline] command = "pardesline" args = ["mcp"] Any HTTP client pardesline mcp --transport streamable-http --port 8765, endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp

When pardesline is not on PATH, use python -m pardesline.mcp_server as the command (same arguments).

docs.title: Tools (all return JSON; errors are {"error", "message", "code"})
docs.text:
Tool What it does list_datasets(tag?, scheme?, medical_only?) the 43 bundled manifests: name, source, licence, roles describe_dataset(ref, count_samples?) roles, licence, citation, layout of a bundled name or any hf://, s3://, tcia://, folder list_samples(ref, limit?, offset?, filters?) paged sample ids, roles, fields; nothing downloaded load_sample(ref, sample, role, standard?) downloads ONE file or DICOM series; returns path, kind, frame, units, labels, license, provenance, accepted methods, and standard_path (PLY / MetaImage) for raw arrays and DICOM folders scan_dataset(ref) draft manifest + questions for a private folder or unknown source confirm_dataset(ref, answers, save_to?) applies the human's answers, loads, saves the manifest export_dataset(ref, folder, take?, overwrite?) standard copy with sidecars and a manifest list_methods(extension?, category?), describe_method(method) the catalog run_method(method, input_path, moving_path?, params?, output_path?, timeout?) one algorithm on a local file, parameters validated first describe_object(path, layout?, kind?) what a local 3D file knows about itself to_mesh(path, label?, isovalue?, output_path?) exact surface of a label map, or an isosurface

Resources: pardesline://datasets (JSON list), pardesline://manifest/{name} (one manifest), pardesline://catalog. Prompt: start_here.

docs.title: The question contract (for the agent)
docs.text: scan_dataset and a premature confirm_dataset return {"error": "NeedsConfirmation", "questions": [{"field": "roles.sweep.layout", "message": ...}], "how_to_answer": ...}. Relay the questions to the human, collect the answers, call confirm_dataset(ref, answers) once. Answer keys: license (SPDX id or free text such as "internal, no redistribution"), pairing, units and frame (one value or {role: value}), labels ({role: {"1": "liver"}}), types ({role: "points" | "mesh" | "volume" | "labels" | "image"}), layout ({role: {"dtype", "shape", "columns", "key"}}). Never invent a licence or a layout; say "unknown" and let the human decide. Gated sources return a FetchError naming the step the human must take (accept terms, set HF_TOKEN).

docs.title: Typical flow
docs.text:
1. list_datasets(medical_only=true) or describe_dataset("tcia://Pancreas-CT").
  2. list_samples(ref, filters={"split": "Tr"}).
  3. load_sample(ref, "la_007", "mask") -> path, labels={"1": "left_atrium"}.
  4. to_mesh(path, label=1) -> surface in LPS mm, or run_method("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_decimate", path, params={"target_reduction": 0.5}).
  5. Tell the user the licence (license_text) before they redistribute anything.

docs.title: Implementation facts
docs.text:
src/pardesline/mcp_server.py, FastMCP from the official mcp SDK (>= 1.2). Tool bodies are synchronous (impl_* functions, testable without a server) and run in a worker thread; build_server() registers them. Tests: tests/test_mcp_server.py (in-process calls and a stdio round trip with the real client).

Source: skills/mcp-server/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Medical volumes: NIfTI, DICOM, MetaImage, label maps
Medical volumes
docs.text: Requires pip install "pardesline[medical]" (SimpleITK + PyVista). .vti outputs are written by every SimpleITK op and read back through the PyVista adapter; a sibling .mha next to a .vti is preferred when present (3x faster).

docs.title: Load
docs.text:
ct = pl.load("ct.nii.gz")  # Volume; frame "LPS, mm (file)", affine from the header
ct = pl.load("/data/p01/dicom")  # a DICOM folder (one series) is a Volume too
ct.info()  # size (x,y,z), spacing, origin, direction, pixel_type, components, affine
img = ct.to_sitk()  # SimpleITK.Image
arr = ct.to_numpy()  # (z, y, x) - SimpleITK convention

SimpleITK loads every format into LPS millimetres (NIfTI RAS is converted), which is why the package states LPS/mm for these files. Index to world is world = direction * spacing * index + origin (ct.frame.affine).

docs.title: Registration (two inputs: input fixed, moving moving)
docs.text:
moved = ct.align(mr)  # rigid, GEOMETRY initialisation (centres aligned)
moved = ct.run(
    "simpleitk_registration.affine", moving=mr, num_iterations=300, metric="mattes_mutual_information"
)
moved = ct.run("simpleitk_registration.bspline", moving=moved, grid_spacing=50.0)
moved = ct.run(
    "simpleitk_registration.advanced_rigid", moving=mr
)  # exhaustive rotation search first: slow, handles large rotations
diff = ct.run(
    "simpleitk_registration.difference_analysis", moving=moved
)  # difference volume + statistics in the sidecar
moved.transform  # {"rotation_deg": [...], "translation_mm": [...], "matrix_3x3": ...} from <output>.json
moved.registration_sidecar  # the whole JSON (metric values, iterations ...)

Shared registration parameters (print with pl.describe("simpleitk_registration.rigid")): num_iterations, learning_rate, sampling_percentage, metric (mattes_mutual_information | mean_squares | correlation | joint_histogram_mi), initializer (GEOMETRY | MOMENTS), sampling_strategy, interpolator, shrink_factors="4,2,1", smoothing_sigmas="2,1,0", number_of_histogram_bins. Use GEOMETRY (aligns image centres); MOMENTS (mass centres) can fail on partial fields of view. Mutual information for multimodal pairs (CT/MR), mean squares for same modality. Deformable: bspline(grid_spacing), demons(num_iterations, standard_deviations). Rigid first, then affine, then B-spline.

Passing moving is mandatory; the scripts' self-alignment demo mode is not reachable through the package.

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text:
mask = ct.segment()  # Otsu -> LabelMap {1: "foreground"}
mask = ct.segment(lower=200, upper=600)  # manual_threshold in intensity units (HU for CT)
mask = mask.run("simpleitk_segmentation.connected_components", min_size=500)  # keep components >= 500 voxels
ws = mask.run("simpleitk_segmentation.watershed", seed_radius=10.0)
mask = mask.with_labels({1: "bone"})  # name the label

Volume.segment always returns a LabelMap. Other outputs are Volumes: declare them with as_labels({...}) when they are label maps.

docs.title: Label map to surface (exact, world coordinates)
docs.text:
bone = mask.to_mesh(label=1)  # .ply, LPS mm; provenance step op="volume_to_mesh", exact=True
bone = bone.decimate(target_reduction=0.8).smooth(n_iterations=20)
bone.save("bone.stl")  # sidecar keeps frame LPS/mm, licence, every step

Marching cubes at 0.5 on the binary voxel == label, through PyVista with the direction matrix applied, triangulated, no attributes. For a grey-level isosurface use ct.to_mesh(isovalue=300). Vertices are in the volume's physical frame, so a surface and its volume overlay directly.

docs.title: The function library (from pardesline import medical)
docs.text:
I/O: load_volume(path) (MHA/NRRD/NIfTI/VTI...), load_dicom(folder) (largest series, size-grouping fallback), save_volume, volume_to_vti, volume_metadata, numpy_to_volume(array, reference), volume_to_binary. Transforms: save_transform, load_transform, transform_to_dict (composite transforms cannot be saved as .tfm; the JSON dict is the portable form), apply_transform(volume, transform, reference), get_initial_transform(fixed, moving, mode). Registration: register_rigid, register_rigid_advanced, register_affine, register_bspline, register_demons, compute_difference_image, compute_difference_thresholded. Segmentation: threshold_otsu, threshold_manual, segment_region_growing, segment_watershed, connected_components, resample, smooth_gaussian.

These are the exact functions the hosted registration studio runs.

docs.title: Gotchas
docs.text:
• sitk.ReadImage cannot open .vti; use medical.load_volume (or obj.to_sitk()), which routes VTK grids through PyVista.
  • Arrays are (z, y, x); img.GetSize() is (x, y, z).
  • A DICOM folder given to an op is materialised once as .mha in pl.output_dir().
  • Datasets: rire_brain (CT/MR pair), popi_lung_4dct (6 phases + mask), liver_tumor_patient01 (CT + 3 observer masks), visible_human_head_mri.

Source: skills/medical-volumes/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-10.

docs.title: Rigid CT / MR registration with SimpleITK
docs.text: Reference scripts: rigid_ct_mr.py.

docs.title: The problem in one line
docs.text: Find the rigid transform T (3 rotations + 3 translations, Euler3DTransform) such that the moving image resampled through T lines up with the fixed image, when the two modalities do not share intensities: bone is bright in CT (+1000 HU) and dark in T1 MRI, CSF is dark in CT and bright in T2. Mean squares or correlation assume a linear intensity relation and fail; mutual information only assumes a statistical dependence between the two intensity distributions.

docs.title: The stack, component by component
docs.text:
Component Setting Why Transform Euler3DTransform initialised with CenteredTransformInitializer 6 DoF; the rotation centre at the fixed image centre (GEOMETRY) or the intensity centre of mass (MOMENTS) so rotations do not sweep the volume out of view Metric MattesMutualInformation, 50 bins Parzen-window joint histogram; 32-64 bins is the sweet spot (fewer = smooth but blurry, more = noisy) Sampling RANDOM, 1-15 % of voxels, fixed seed MI on all voxels is slow and over-fits noise; random sampling adds stochasticity that helps escape local minima Optimizer RegularStepGradientDescent or GradientDescent (lr 1.0 then 0.2), SetOptimizerScalesFromPhysicalShift rotations (rad) and translations (mm) have different sensitivities: physical-shift scales equalise them Multi-resolution shrink 4,2,1 with smoothing sigmas 2,1,0 mm capture-range at coarse levels, precision at fine; sigmas in physical units so anisotropic voxels are handled Interpolator linear during optimisation, linear for the final image, nearest for labels, B-spline for the final image when quality matters Convergence minimum value 1e-6 over a 10-iteration window, 100-500 iterations watch the metric curve: a plateau in the first 20 iterations means the capture range was missed

In pardesline every one of these is a parameter of simpleitk_registration.rigid:

import pardesline as pl

ds = pl.load("rire_brain")  # CT + MR-T1 of one brain, LPS mm
s = ds[0]
moved = s.ct.align(
    s.mr_t1,  # fixed = CT, moving = MR
    metric="mattes_mutual_information",
    number_of_histogram_bins=50,
    initializer="GEOMETRY",
    sampling_strategy="RANDOM",
    sampling_percentage=0.05,
    learning_rate=1.0,
    num_iterations=200,
    shrink_factors="4,2,1",
    smoothing_sigmas="2,1,0",
    smoothing_sigmas_in_physical_units=True,
    optimizer_scales_from_physical_shift=True,
    interpolator="LINEAR",
)
moved.transform  # rotation_deg, translation_mm, matrix_4x4, final metric

simpleitk_registration.advanced_rigid adds an exhaustive rotation search (exhaustive_steps_per_axis, phase 1) before gradient descent: use it when the initial misalignment exceeds ~30 deg or when the two scans were acquired in different patient positions. simpleitk_registration.affine adds scale and shear (12 DoF) for scanner calibration differences; bspline and demons are deformable (see the bottom of this page).

docs.title: Frames: the part that breaks silently
docs.text:
• DICOM and every ITK reader give LPS millimetres with origin, spacing and direction cosines; NIfTI headers are RAS and ITK converts them on read. pardesline's Volume.frame carries the affine; the registration operates in physical space, so two volumes with different spacing and orientation register without resampling first.
  • Never register voxel arrays (GetArrayFromImage) directly: you would lose the geometry and the transform would be meaningless in the scanner frame.
  • The output transform maps fixed physical points to moving physical points (ITK convention). To move an annotation from fixed to moving, apply T; to bring the moving image onto the fixed grid, Resample(moving, fixed, T). Label maps: nearest-neighbour interpolation, defaultPixelValue=0.
  • Composite registrations (rigid then B-spline): CompositeTransform, applied inner-to-outer; keep each stage's transform file (.tfm).

docs.title: Diagnostics and validation
docs.text:
1. Plot the metric per iteration (SimpleITK AddCommand(sitkIterationEvent)), check it decreases at each level and the level changes are visible.
  2. Checkerboard and colour overlay of fixed vs resampled moving (simpleitk_registration.difference_analysis gives a difference map).
  3. Target registration error on 5-10 anatomical landmarks placed independently in both volumes (not used by the algorithm): ||T(p_fixed) - p_moving|| in mm; sub-voxel on rigid brain CT/MR (RIRE reports ~1 mm).
  4. Dice of propagated masks when segmentations exist (skull, ventricles).
  5. Run twice with different random seeds / sampling: a stable result moves by less than the voxel size; otherwise increase sampling or bins.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix Metric flat, no motion capture range missed, initial misalignment too large MOMENTS initializer, advanced_rigid exhaustive search, coarser first level (shrink 8) Converges to a wrong but plausible pose local minimum of MI (symmetric head, repeated vertebrae) multi-start, more bins, larger sampling, mask the field of view to the common anatomy Drifts with iterations learning rate too high 0.2-0.5 with physical-shift scales; RegularStepGradientDescent with relaxation Good at centre, bad at edges not rigid: scanner distortion, patient deformation affine then B-spline (grid_spacing 30-50 mm) PET-CT off by a slice different acquisition times / breathing rigid on the torso mask only, then deformable Works on brain, fails on abdomen organs move independently mask the organ of interest; deformable (demons for same-modality, B-spline MI for multimodal)

docs.title: Going deformable
docs.text:
• simpleitk_registration.bspline: B-spline FFD on a control-point grid (grid_spacing mm, multi-resolution scale_factors), LBFGSB, MI for multimodal. Validate with the Jacobian determinant (no folding) and TRE.
  • simpleitk_registration.demons: diffeomorphic demons on same-modality images (intensities must match), standard_deviations smooth the update field; fast, dense, not for CT-MR.
  • Always rigid (or affine) first; deformable models should correct millimetres, not centimetres.

docs.title: Datasets to practise on
docs.text:
rire_brain (CT + MR-T1, the reference multimodal pair), popi_lung_4dct (same-modality breathing phases: rigid then B-spline/demons), ixi_brain_mri (T1 vs T2 vs PD of the same subject), chaos_abdomen (CT and MR of different patients: atlas-style registration), tcia_nsclc_radiomics_dicom (DICOM series as input), hf_openmind (T1 vs T2).

scripts/rigid_ct_mr.py registers the RIRE pair through pardesline, repeats the registration directly with SimpleITK to expose every setting, exports the checkerboard, and reports the metric trace and the transform.

Source: skills/multimodal-rigid-registration/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: The object model: PointCloud, Mesh, Volume, LabelMap
The object model
docs.text:
import pardesline as pl

ct = pl.load("ct.mha")  # Volume
ct.kind  # "volume"
ct.frame.describe()  # "LPS, mm (file)"   <- read from the header
ct.frame.affine  # 4x4 index->world, from origin/spacing/direction
ct.info()  # {"size": (512,512,29), "spacing": (...), "pixel_type": "16-bit signed integer", ...}
ct.license.describe()  # "unknown licence" until declared

docs.title: Kinds and classes (by extension; .nii.gz aware; a DICOM folder is a Volume)
docs.text: Class kind extensions PointCloud pointcloud .ply .pcd .xyz .txt .pts .las .laz Mesh mesh .stl .obj .off .glb .gltf .vtp (a .ply with faces still loads as PointCloud; to_open3d() returns the mesh) Volume volume .vti .vtu .vtk .mha .mhd .nrrd .nii .nii.gz .dcm (file or folder) LabelMap labels any volume with labels declared, a kind: labels sidecar, a labels role, or Volume.segment() / as_labels() Transform transform .tfm .h5 .hdf5 .mat Image image .png .jpg .tif .bmp RawArray array .npy .npz .bin .raw: numbers without meaning until a layout says what they are (see below) Object file anything else

docs.title: Raw arrays: a layout, never a guess
docs.text:
raw = pl.load("sweep.bin")  # RawArray; .to_numpy() / ops raise until a layout is declared
sweep = raw.as_points(dtype="float32", shape="(N,4)", columns=["x", "y", "z", "reflectance"])  # PointCloud
sweep = pl.load("sweep.bin", layout={"dtype": "float32", "shape": "(N,4)", "columns": [...]})  # same
grid = pl.load(
    "occ.npz", layout={"key": "occ_label", "shape": "(200,200,16)", "spacing": [0.4] * 3}, kind="labels"
)
occ = raw.as_volume(labels={1: "car"}, key="occ_label", shape="(200,200,16)")  # LabelMap

shape "(N,k)" means points (columns name x, y, z and attributes), "(a,b,c)" a dense grid (x, y, z order; spacing / origin in the role's units, else unit spacing with a warning); dtype is required for headerless .bin; key picks the array in an .npz; scale rescales colours. The layout is kept in obj.layout, saved in the sidecar, and with_layout(...) amends it. Before any op or hand-off the array is materialised once into a standard file through the layout (PLY for points, MetaImage for grids): obj._op_input(), to_open3d(), to_sitk(), info() use it, and obj.save("sweep.ply") writes that standard file instead of the raw one. A .bin with a wrong layout fails with "do not split into rows" or "does not match layout.shape", never with silent garbage.

docs.title: Frame: file > format > manifest > user, never a guess
docs.text:
obj.frame is a Frame(axes, units, affine, crs, source).

  • Volumes readable by SimpleITK (.mha .mhd .nrrd .nii .nii.gz .dcm): axes="LPS", units="mm", affine from the header, source="file". NIfTI RAS headers are converted by ITK, so the loaded data is LPS.
  • glTF (.glb .gltf): Y-up, m, source="format".
  • Everything else: axes=None, units=None (frame.known is False). VTK grids (.vti) carry spacing/origin but no convention.
  • Declaring: obj.with_frame("Z-up", "mm") returns a copy with source="user"; it fills unknowns and does not override what a header stated (a warning is logged if a manifest contradicts the file). Manifest roles fill frames with source="manifest".
  • obj.units, obj.axes are shortcuts.

docs.title: Labels and licence
docs.text:
mask = pl.load("seg.nii.gz").with_labels({1: "liver", 2: "tumor"})  # -> LabelMap
mask.labels, mask.label_id("tumor")  # {1:'liver',2:'tumor'}, 2
obj = obj.with_license("CC-BY-4.0")  # or a dict / pl.License(...)
obj.license.spdx, obj.license.commercial, obj.license.known

pl.License(spdx, commercial, source_url, note, requires_agreement, redistribution).

docs.title: Provenance and the sidecar
docs.text:
Every run() / conversion returns a new Object whose provenance is the input's list plus one step dict (step: "run"|"convert"|"load", module, method, params as sent, input, moving, output, duration_s, pardesline version, timestamp; for conversions op, label/isovalue, exact). Registration outputs expose obj.transform (parsed <output>.json) and obj.registration_sidecar.

obj.save(dest) copies the file (plus .raw sibling for .mhd, plus the registration .json) and writes <dest>.pardesline.json with kind, frame, labels, layout, licence, role and provenance. A raw array saved under a standard extension (.ply, .mha) is decoded through its layout; a DICOM folder saved as .mha is written as one volume. pl.load(dest) reads it back, so the frame and labels survive a round trip. dest ending with / or an existing folder keeps the file name. sidecar=False skips it.

docs.title: Running algorithms on an object
docs.text:
cloud = pl.load("scan.ply").with_frame("sensor", "m")
clean = cloud.downsample(voxel_size=0.01).remove_outliers(nb_neighbors=20, std_ratio=2.0)
surf = clean.normals().poisson(depth=9).decimate(target_reduction=0.5)
surf.run("pyvista_mesh_processing.pv_fill_holes", hole_size=10.0)

obj.run(method, /, *, moving=None, output=None, timeout=None, on_log=None, on_progress=None, **params). method is "module.method", a bare id that is unique for the file type, or an alias. The result inherits frame (affine dropped: ops write new geometry) and license; labels are not propagated. obj.methods() lists the qualified names that accept the file; a DICOM folder is materialised as .mha once before ops run on it.

Aliases (explicit methods): downsample, remove_outliers, normals, poisson, ball_pivoting, icp(moving), ransac(moving), decimate, smooth, to_points, register(moving), segment.

docs.title: Conversions named after the job
docs.text:
Call On What it does Exact? Volume.segment() Volume Otsu threshold (otsu_threshold) -> LabelMap with {1: "foreground"} - Volume.segment(lower=, upper=) Volume manual_threshold in intensity units -> LabelMap - Volume.as_labels({1: "liver"}) Volume declare an existing volume a label map - LabelMap.to_mesh(label=k) LabelMap boundary of voxels == k, in world coordinates (spacing, origin, direction cosines applied), .ply yes (in-process marching cubes at 0.5) LabelMap.to_mesh() LabelMap with a single named label same, that label yes Volume.to_mesh(isovalue=v) Volume level set of a grey-level volume parametric Mesh.to_points(num_points=5000) Mesh Poisson-disk sampling (mesh_to_pcd_poisson_disk) exact sampling PointCloud.to_mesh(depth=9, ...) PointCloud Poisson reconstruction, density-trimmed (poisson) lossy, parametric PointCloud.align(moving) PointCloud RANSAC on FPFH then ICP (ransac_icp_pipeline); transform in .transform - Volume.align(moving) Volume rigid SimpleITK registration (rigid, GEOMETRY init) - PointCloud.clean() / Mesh.clean() statistical_outlier_removal / pv_clean - PointCloud.segment(eps=, min_points=) PointCloud DBSCAN clusters as colours (dbscan_clustering) -

Wording for surfaces from points: "a clean, density-trimmed surface", never "watertight". to_mesh on a volume requires exactly one of label / isovalue: the package never picks a level.

docs.title: Hand-offs
docs.text:
obj.to_open3d() (PointCloud or TriangleMesh), obj.to_pyvista() (pv.read), obj.to_sitk() (SimpleITK image, DICOM folders accepted, VTI through the PyVista adapter), obj.to_numpy() (points, vertices, or voxels as (z, y, x)). os.fspath(obj) gives the path, so any library reader accepts the object directly. Each raises pl.MissingDependency naming the extra.

Source: skills/object-model/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Point cloud registration with RANSAC, FPFH and ICP
docs.text: Reference scripts: registration_eval.py.

docs.title: Point-cloud registration: RANSAC + FPFH + ICP, done properly
The pipeline and why two stages
docs.text:
A single ICP converges only from a nearby pose (typically < 30 deg, < one object radius). The global stage finds that pose from features; the local stage polishes it.

downsample (voxel v)  ->  normals (r_n = 2v)  ->  FPFH (r_f = 5v)
      ->  RANSAC on feature correspondences (d_max = 1.5v)   [global, coarse]
      ->  ICP point-to-plane on the full-resolution clouds (d_max = 0.4v)   [local, fine]
      ->  metrics: fitness, inlier RMSE, transform T (4x4)

Everything scales with one number, the voxel size v, which should be 2-5 times the point spacing and about 1 % of the object's bounding-box diagonal (pardesline's voxel_size=0 picks 1.3 % of the diagonal, the Open3D tutorial setting). If the units are wrong (mm vs m) every radius is wrong: check cloud.frame.describe() first.

docs.title: FPFH in two sentences
docs.text: For each point, the Simplified Point Feature Histogram encodes the angles (alpha, phi, theta of the Darboux frame) between its normal and the normals of neighbours within r_f; FPFH re-weights each point's SPFH with its neighbours' SPFHs (1/d weights), giving a 33-bin histogram that is rotation-invariant and cheap (O(N k)). It needs normals that are consistently oriented; estimate them on the downsampled cloud with r_n = 2v, max_nn=30.

docs.title: RANSAC on correspondences
docs.text: Sample n = 3 correspondences by feature matching (mutual filter on: both directions must agree), estimate a rigid transform (Umeyama / SVD), prune with the edge-length checker (edge_length_threshold = 0.9: the three pairwise distances must agree within 10 %) and the distance checker (d_max = 1.5v), count inliers. Stop after max_iteration (100 000) or when the confidence (0.999) is reached. Output: T_ransac, fitness (inlier fraction of the source), inlier RMSE.

docs.title: ICP refinement
docs.text: Point-to-plane minimises sum ((R p_i + t - q_i) · n_qi)^2 - it converges in far fewer iterations than point-to-point and slides along surfaces instead of fighting them; it needs target normals. Point-to-point is the fallback when normals are unreliable (sparse, noisy LiDAR). Correspondence distance 0.4v on the full-resolution clouds; stop on relative_fitness and relative_rmse below 1e-6 or at max_iteration. Generalised ICP (plane-to-plane, covariance-weighted) and robust kernels (Tukey, Cauchy on the residual) help with outliers; multi-scale ICP (v, v/2, v/4) helps with large residual error after RANSAC.

docs.title: Parameters, by name, in pardesline
docs.text:
import pardesline as pl

fixed = pl.load("scan.ply").with_frame("sensor", "mm")
moving = pl.load("atlas.ply").with_frame("sensor", "mm")

aligned = fixed.align(moving)  # registration.ransac_icp_pipeline, voxel_size auto
aligned = fixed.run(
    "registration.ransac_icp_pipeline",
    moving=moving,
    voxel_size=2.0,  # mm; 2-5x the point spacing
    normal_radius_factor=2.0,
    fpfh_radius_factor=5.0,
    distance_threshold_factor=1.5,
    mutual_filter=True,
    ransac_n=3,
    edge_length_threshold=0.9,
    ransac_max_iteration=100000,
    ransac_confidence=0.999,
    icp_threshold_factor=0.4,
    icp_estimation_method="point_to_plane",
    icp_max_iteration=30,
    icp_relative_fitness=1e-6,
    icp_relative_rmse=1e-6,
)
aligned.transform  # {'fitness', 'inlier_rmse', 'transformation_matrix', ...} from <output>.json

Two-stage control: registration.ransac_global alone (coarse pose, to inspect before refining) and registration.icp_refinement (which runs its own RANSAC pre-pass unless the clouds already overlap: ransac_seed_fitness is the fitness below which it falls back to a centre-of-mass initialisation). Set ransac_with_scaling=True only when the two clouds come from different devices with unknown scale (photogrammetry vs scanner); never for LiDAR.

Parameter effects, from experience:

Symptom Likely cause Change RANSAC fitness < 0.3, ICP does nothing features meaningless: v too small (noise) or too large (no detail) scan v over 0.5x-4x; check units Converges to a mirrored / rotated pose symmetric object (sphere, cylinder, vertebra body) add landmarks or a prior pose; use ransac_n=4; verify with TRE, not fitness Fitness high, RMSE high correspondence distance too generous lower icp_threshold_factor to 0.2-0.3 Fitness drops when overlap is partial fitness counts source points; partial overlap caps it judge by inlier RMSE and pose error on the overlapping region; crop first Drift on flat scenes (floors, walls) point-to-plane slides along planes point-to-point, or add walls/edges, or constrain DoF Different scale mm vs m, or photogrammetry ransac_with_scaling=True, then fix the scale and re-run rigid

docs.title: Metrics: which ones mean something
docs.text:
• Fitness = inliers / source points at distance d_max. Depends on d_max; compare runs only at the same threshold. Caps at the overlap ratio.
  • Inlier RMSE = RMS distance of inliers. Lower bound is the noise level of the scanner (0.5 mm for the ultrasound use case): below that you are measuring noise, not alignment.
  • Pose error against a known transform (synthetic tests, phantoms): rotation error arccos((tr(R_est R_true^T) - 1) / 2) in degrees, translation error at the object centre ||T_est c - T_true c|| (not the raw translation vector, which mixes with rotation about the origin).
  • Target registration error (TRE): distance between corresponding landmarks not used by the algorithm. The only metric a clinician accepts.
  • Chamfer / Hausdorff between the aligned surfaces: see the evaluation-metrics-3d skill. Hausdorff is dominated by one outlier; report the 95th percentile.

scripts/registration_eval.py runs the full pipeline on a bundled cloud with a known synthetic transform and prints all of these.

docs.title: Non-rigid: Coherent Point Drift
docs.text: CPD treats the moving cloud as Gaussian mixture centroids and the fixed cloud as samples; EM alternates responsibilities and a displacement field that is regularised to be smooth (beta = kernel width, lambda_val = regularisation weight, w = outlier fraction). deformable_registration.cpd_deformable exposes them; low_rank=True with num_eig makes it tractable above ~10 k points. Use it after a rigid alignment, for organ motion, breathing, or atlas-to-patient shape adaptation; never as a first stage. Validate with Jacobian-determinant positivity of the displacement (no folding) and TRE.

docs.title: Medical specifics
docs.text:
• Atlas to patient (see atlas-label-transfer): the scan is the fixed reference, the atlas moves. Labels travel with point order, so keep the atlas point order (pardesline's output keeps it).
  • Ultrasound reconstructions are noisy and partial: v 2-3 mm, point-to-plane, expect fitness 0.6-0.9, RMSE near the noise floor.
  • CBCT / intra-oral scans: 0.1-0.2 mm spacing, v 0.5 mm; symmetric teeth need the arch as context, never a single tooth.
  • Multimodal volumes (CT vs MR) are not a point-cloud problem: use intensity-based registration (multimodal-rigid-registration skill).

docs.title: Datasets to practise on
docs.text:
open3d_icp_demo (indoor fragments, sensor frame, m), open3d_bunny (synthetic transforms), kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001 (consecutive sweeps, sensor frame, m; odometry-style), medshapenet (two instances of the same organ for shape registration), c3vd_endoscopy_splats (points role).

ds = pl.load("open3d_icp_demo")
pair = ds["pair_0_1"]
moved = pair.target.align(pair.source, voxel_size=0.05)  # metres
print(moved.transform["fitness"], moved.transform["inlier_rmse"])

Source: skills/point-cloud-registration/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Scanning a private folder into a manifest
Scanning a private folder
docs.text:
import pardesline as pl

pl.load("/data/study_A")

raises pl.NeedsConfirmation:

study_a: 4 question(s) before this folder can be loaded:
  - license: Who owns this data and under which terms may it be used? (e.g. 'internal, no redistribution', 'CC-BY-4.0')
  - roles.ct.units: p01/ct/scan.vti: the format carries no unit. mm, m, ...?
  - roles.surface.units: p01/surface.stl: the format carries no unit. mm, m, ...?
  - roles.mask.labels: p01/masks/liver.vti looks like a label map (name hint). What does each value mean? e.g. {1: 'liver'}
Answer in the call, e.g.
  pl.load(folder, license='internal, no redistribution', units={'ct': 'mm', 'surface': 'mm'}, labels={'mask': {1: 'organ'}})
or edit the saved draft, or pass assume=True to proceed with unknowns, or interactive=True.
Draft saved: /data/study_A/pardesline.manifest.json

The exception carries .questions (list of Question(field, message, suggestion)), .manifest (the draft) and .draft_path.

docs.title: What the scan does (so you can predict its output)
docs.text:
1. Collects data files by extension (point clouds, meshes, volumes, images, transforms); a folder containing .dcm / .ima files is one volume entry. Hidden entries, .txt, archives and .pardesline.json sidecars are ignored (declare them by hand if needed).
  2. Groups into samples, in this order of preference: folder (every top-level sub-folder is a sample: p01/, p02/), name_prefix (flat folder with <id>_<role> / <id>-<role> names repeating across ids: a_image.vti, a_seg.vti, b_image.vti, ...), file (each file its own sample). A pairing question is raised when the confidence is low.
  3. Names roles after the containing sub-folder (ct/, masks/ -> mask, images/ -> image), the file stem for a file directly in the sample folder (p01/surface.stl -> surface), the name suffix for name_prefix, else the type (volume, mesh, points). Duplicates get _2, _3.
  4. Types a volume as labels when its path matches mask|seg|label|gt|ground|annot|roi; otherwise reads the header and, for integer voxels, asks whether it is a label map.
  5. Fills frames it can know: ITK formats -> LPS/mm, glTF -> Y-up/m; asks units (and frame for meshes/points) for the rest.
  6. Asks the licence unless the source states one (a Hub card).
  7. Raw arrays (.npy, .npz, .bin, .raw) become attribute roles with a roles.<role>.layout question: the type and the layout must be declared (types={"sweep": "points"}, layout={"sweep": {...}}).
  8. A folder that wraps everything (raw/p01/...) is stripped before grouping; one folder holding files of different kinds is one sample whose files are its roles, a folder of same-kind files is one sample per file.

pl.scan(folder, name=None, read_headers=True) returns the draft Manifest (.questions, .is_draft, .describe()), without raising. pl.scan("hf://org/name/sub"), pl.scan("s3://bucket/prefix") and pl.scan("tcia://Collection") do the same from a listing (no headers read; the licence comes from the Hub card, OpenNeuro's CC0 policy or TCIA's CC BY 3.0 default, marked TO CONFIRM); the draft is saved under pl.cache_dir()/drafts/ and reused by the next pl.load. When no question remains, pl.load returns the dataset directly.

docs.title: The four ways to answer
docs.text:
1. In the call (idempotent, scriptable):

ds = pl.load(
    "/data/study_A",
    license="internal, no redistribution",  # or an SPDX id "CC-BY-4.0", or a dict
    units="mm",  # one value for every role ...
    frame={"surface": "LPS"},  # ... or per role
    labels={"mask": {1: "liver", 2: "tumor"}},  # per role; {1: "liver"} applies to all label roles
    pairing="folder",
    types={"sweep": "points"},  # raw arrays: what they are ...
    layout={"sweep": {"dtype": "float32", "shape": "(N,4)", "columns": ["x", "y", "z", "i"]}},  # ... and how
)

labels={"mask": None} says "not a label map" (the role becomes volume). A dict whose keys are not roles raises pl.ManifestError listing the roles.

2. Edit the saved draft pardesline.manifest.json (set license, the roles' units / frame / labels, and empty questions), then pl.load(folder) again. The file is a normal manifest: it can be versioned next to the data and shared with colleagues; its source.root is re-pointed to the folder's current location on load.

3. Interactive pl.load(folder, interactive=True): one input() prompt per question; labels are typed as 1: liver, 2: tumor; none means not a label map; empty keeps the suggestion.

4. Assume pl.load(folder, assume=True): loads with unknowns left unknown and one warning per open question. For exploration only; the objects' frame.known is False and license.known is False.

docs.title: For an AI agent
docs.text: Do not answer the questions yourself. Relay err.questions to the human, collect the answers, then call pl.load(folder, **answers) once. If the human cannot answer the licence, use license="internal, terms unknown" rather than inventing an SPDX id, and say the data must not be redistributed. After a successful load, ds.manifest.save(path) keeps the confirmed manifest for the next session.

docs.title: Limits (say them when relevant)
docs.text:
• No reading inside .npy / .npz / .bin: the layout answer (or a manifest with one) is required; pl.load("sweep.bin", layout={...}) for a single file.
  • DICOM series are split per folder, not per SeriesInstanceUID; a folder mixing series loads as one series (the largest) through SimpleITK.
  • .vti headers are read fully (no header-only reader), so the scan of a large VTK folder takes a moment.
  • Pairing heuristics are deliberately simple; when the folder layout is unusual, write the samples list in the manifest by hand.

Source: skills/scanning-private-folders/SKILL.md, one of the twenty skills served by pardesline mcp; published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Using pardesline
docs.text: pardesline (import as pl) is one Python package for point clouds, meshes, medical volumes and label maps. Everything under pl.load / pl.run executes on the machine that runs Python; nothing leaves it. The cloud client is optional and separate (pardesline.cloud).

docs.title: Install (tell the user exactly this)
docs.text:
pip install "pardesline[all]"       # Open3D + PyVista + SimpleITK + huggingface_hub
pip install "pardesline[local]"     # point clouds, meshes, SDF, LiDAR (Open3D, PyVista)
pip install "pardesline[medical]"   # volumes, DICOM, registration, segmentation (SimpleITK + PyVista)
pip install "pardesline[hf]"        # pl.load("hf://...")
pip install pardesline              # catalog + object model + cloud client only, no native libs

Python 3.10 to 3.12 for [local] (Open3D 0.19 has no 3.13 wheels). A missing library raises pl.MissingDependency whose message names the extra to install.

docs.title: The three entry points
docs.text:
import pardesline as pl

obj = pl.load("scan.ply")  # Object (PointCloud / Mesh / Volume / LabelMap ...)
out = obj.run("point_cloud_processing.voxel_downsample", voxel_size=0.02)  # new Object
res = pl.run("point_cloud_processing", "voxel_downsample", "scan.ply", voxel_size=0.02)  # RunResult
ds = pl.load("rire_brain")  # Dataset: samples with typed roles, fetched on access
