docs.title: PointNet segmentation of medical and industrial point clouds in Python
docs.text:
What ships today, and what is coming

Today: make_point_dataset.py (label surfaces to labelled point clouds) and pointnet_seg.py (train / eval / infer, the original PointNet segmentation network). No weights are shipped and there is no inference API: the scripts are reference implementations that read any pardesline dataset.

Coming: one-line model access. The same registry pattern as datasets, a model manifest (source, weights URI, licence, input type, task, memory needs, provenance) and pl.load_model(...) / pl.run(model, dataset). This page keeps its URL. Follow and vote on the model registry tracking issue; model manifests can be contributed now from templates/new_model/.

Reference scripts: make_point_dataset.py, pointnet_seg.py (shipped in the wheel under pardesline/skills/pointnet-segmentation/scripts/, served by the MCP tool get_skill).

Runnable example: examples/pointnet_hippocampus/run.py, executed on 2026-10-16; its outputs are committed next to it.

docs.title: Architecture (segmentation branch), tensor by tensor
docs.text:
input           (N x 3)    xyz, optionally (N x 6) with normals
T-Net(3)        3 x 3      mini-PointNet regresses a transform; x <- x @ T          input alignment
shared MLP      (N x 64) -> (N x 64)                                                 per-point, Conv1d k=1
T-Net(64)       64 x 64    + regulariser L_reg = || I - A A^T ||_F^2 (weight 1e-3)  feature alignment
shared MLP      (N x 64) -> (N x 128) -> (N x 1024)
max-pool        (1 x 1024)  symmetric function: order-invariant global descriptor
broadcast+concat (N x 1088) = local 64-d  ++  global 1024-d                          every point sees the shape
seg head        (N x 512) -> (N x 256) -> (N x 128) -> (N x K)  softmax per point

Why it works: a shared MLP applied per point followed by a symmetric pooling is invariant to the point order (f({x_i}) = gamma(max_i h(x_i))); the T-Nets learn a canonical pose so the network does not have to see every rotation; the global feature acts as context memory for each point. What it cannot do: capture local neighbourhoods (two points 1 mm apart are processed independently until the global pooling), hence boundaries between adjacent teeth or vertebrae come out ragged.

PointNet++ fixes that with set-abstraction levels: farthest-point sampling of centroids, ball query (radius r) grouping, a mini-PointNet per group, repeated 3 times with growing radii (0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 in the unit sphere), then feature propagation (interpolation + skip links) back to all points for segmentation. Multi-scale grouping (MSG) uses several radii per level for density robustness. Modern successors (Point Transformer v3, PointNeXt) keep the same data contract; start with PointNet++ unless you have 10 k+ labelled clouds.

docs.title: Data contract
docs.text: Item Value Points per cloud 2048 (parts, teeth) to 4096-8192 (organs, scenes); sample with FPS or Poisson-disk, pad by repetition Features xyz; add normals (N x 6) for surfaces, intensity for LiDAR, HU for CT-derived points Normalisation subtract the centroid, divide by the max radius (unit sphere) per cloud; store the scale and centroid to map predictions back Labels one integer per point, 0..K-1, with a class table; -1 = ignore Augmentation random rotation about the up axis (or full SO(3) when poses are arbitrary), jitter sigma 0.01 clipped at 0.05, random scale 0.8-1.25, point dropout Split by patient / object, never by cloud of the same object

docs.title: Labelled clouds from pardesline datasets
docs.text: scripts/make_point_dataset.py turns any dataset with label roles into .npz training clouds: for each sample it extracts the surface of each label (LabelMap.to_mesh(label=k)), samples it (Mesh.to_points, Poisson-disk, face normals), tags the points with k, merges the structures, normalises, and writes points (N,6) float32, labels (N,) int64, centroid, scale, frame. Works on msd_task04_hippocampus (anterior / posterior), amos22 (15 organs), totalsegmentator_ct (pick the organ roles), verse19_spine (vertebra ids), medshapenet meshes (one structure per file: label by file), and your own folder after pl.scan. CBCT teeth: segment the arch with simpleitk_segmentation.manual_threshold on HU, LabelMap.to_mesh, then label points by tooth from an existing annotation.

docs.title: Training recipe
docs.text:
• Loss: cross-entropy with class weights 1 / log(1.2 + freq) (or Dice + CE) plus 1e-3 * L_reg; label smoothing 0.1 helps on noisy boundaries.
  • Adam lr 1e-3, batch 16-32, 200 epochs, lr x0.5 every 20 epochs (or cosine); batch-norm momentum decayed; dropout 0.5 before the last layers.
  • Mixed precision is fine; a 2048-point PointNet trains in ~1 h on one GPU for 5 k clouds.
  • Monitor per-class IoU on a patient-level validation split; mIoU is the headline, the smallest class is the story.
  • Pretrained weights (ShapeNet part segmentation) help only for the first epochs; medical shapes differ enough that training from scratch with augmentation is usually as good.

scripts/pointnet_seg.py is a complete PyTorch reference (model, dataset loader for the .npz contract, training loop, evaluation, inference that writes a labelled PLY readable by pardesline). It needs torch.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text: Per-class IoU and mIoU on points; because sampling is uniform, points-IoU approximates surface-area IoU. Add a boundary error: fraction of mislabelled points within 1 mm of a label boundary vs away from it, to distinguish "ragged edges" from "wrong structure". For volumes of structures (teeth, chambers): reconstruct per label (atlas-label-transfer skill) and compare volumes.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix mIoU stuck ~ majority class class imbalance, lr too high class weights, Dice term, lr 1e-4 warm-up Rotated test clouds fail training poses too uniform; T-Net not enough full SO(3) augmentation, or canonicalise with PCA / a registration step before the network Ragged boundaries between neighbours no local features (PointNet) PointNet++ / k-NN graph, add normals, post-process by majority vote in a 1 mm neighbourhood Good on train, bad on new scanner density / noise shift voxel-downsample to a fixed spacing before sampling, noise augmentation Tiny structures vanish 2048 points too few for them more points, or crop per region, or oversample points on small classes

docs.title: Inference back to objects
docs.text:
import numpy as np, pardesline as pl

cloud = pl.load("arch.ply").with_frame("LPS", "mm")
xyz = cloud.to_numpy()  # (N,3)
# ... normalise, forward, argmax -> labels (N,)
from pardesline.object.arrays import write_ply

out = pl.load(write_ply("arch_labelled.ply", xyz, {"label": labels}))  # label as a per-point property

Datasets: msd_task04_hippocampus, amos22, totalsegmentator_ct, verse19_spine, medshapenet, hf_kitti360_gs_subset (points + point_segments for scene segmentation), kitti_raw_2011_09_26_drive_0001.

Source: skills/pointnet-segmentation/SKILL.md, published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: VAE anomaly detection on medical images in Python
docs.text:
What ships today, and what is coming

Today: vae_anomaly.py: train on normal images, score any image by reconstruction residual, AUROC when labels exist. No weights are shipped and there is no inference API: the scripts are reference implementations that read any pardesline dataset.

Coming: one-line model access. The same registry pattern as datasets, a model manifest (source, weights URI, licence, input type, task, memory needs, provenance) and pl.load_model(...) / pl.run(model, dataset). This page keeps its URL. Follow and vote on the model registry tracking issue; model manifests can be contributed now from templates/new_model/.

Reference scripts: vae_anomaly.py (shipped in the wheel under pardesline/skills/vae-anomaly-detection/scripts/, served by the MCP tool get_skill).

Runnable example: examples/vae_anomaly_hippocampus/run.py, executed on 2026-10-16; its outputs are committed next to it.

docs.title: Reconstruction-based anomaly detection with a VAE
The idea
docs.text: Train a model that only knows normal data. At test time it reconstructs the normal part of an input and smooths away what it has never seen; the residual |x - x_hat| highlights the anomaly without a single abnormal training example. "A model that only knows healthy teeth reveals the cavity."

docs.title: The VAE
docs.text:
Encoder q(z|x) = N(mu(x), diag(sigma^2(x))), decoder p(x|z), loss

L = E_q[ -log p(x|z) ]  +  beta * KL( q(z|x) || N(0, I) )
  = reconstruction (L2 / BCE / SSIM)  +  beta * 1/2 sum (mu^2 + sigma^2 - log sigma^2 - 1)

with the reparameterisation z = mu + sigma * eps. The KL term makes the latent space smooth and prevents the identity mapping; beta sets the trade-off: beta < 1 sharper reconstructions, weaker regularisation; beta > 1 (beta-VAE) more disentangled, blurrier. For anomaly detection a slightly under-capacity model is the point: it must not be able to reconstruct the anomaly.

Reference design (dental panoramic X-ray, 1 x 256 x 256): encoder of 5 blocks Conv2d(3x3, stride 2) + BatchNorm + ReLU (32-64-128-256-512 channels) to 8 x 8, fully connected to mu, logvar of 512 dims; decoder mirrors with ConvTranspose2d; sigmoid output; loss L2 (or BCE) + KL; Adam 1e-3 to 1e-4, batch 32, 100-300 epochs; cyclic or warm-up annealing of beta (0 -> 1 over 10 epochs) avoids posterior collapse. For volumes: 3D convolutions on 64^3 or 96^3 patches, latent 256-1024.

docs.title: Residual maps and scores
docs.text:
1. r = |x - x_hat| (or 1 - SSIM map, which is less sensitive to small intensity shifts).
  2. Smooth with a Gaussian (sigma 2-4 px) to suppress pixel noise.
  3. Image score = mean of the top 1 % of r (or the 99th percentile); pixel map = r thresholded.
  4. Threshold from the validation set of normal images: e.g. the 99th percentile of normal scores for a 1 % false-positive rate; never from the test set.
  5. Morphological opening removes 1-2 px specks; keep components above a minimum area in physical units (mm^2 via the pixel spacing).

Variants that help: masking the field of view (teeth region only), averaging residuals over several latent samples (the VAE is stochastic), comparing against the k nearest normal training images instead of a single reconstruction.

docs.title: Evaluation (see evaluation-metrics-3d)
docs.text:
• Image level: AUROC and AUPRC of the score on a test set with both classes.
  • Pixel level: AUROC / AUPRC on pixels when masks exist (AUPRC is the honest one at 1 % anomaly pixels), Dice of the thresholded map at the chosen operating point, per-lesion detection rate at an IoU of 0.3.
  • Baselines to beat: a Gaussian on raw pixels, PCA reconstruction, k-NN on DINOv3 features (dinov3-dense-features); report them.

docs.title: Honest limits
docs.text:
• The decoder may reconstruct the anomaly when it is large or low-frequency (a bright implant is "easy"): the score then drops. Limit capacity, add noise or masking to the input (denoising / inpainting VAE).
  • Blurry reconstructions produce residuals on every edge: SSIM or perceptual losses, or compare at a lower resolution.
  • Domain shift (another scanner, exposure) raises every score: normalise intensities, calibrate thresholds per site, monitor the score distribution.
  • Subtle anomalies below the reconstruction error floor are invisible; report the floor (mean residual on normal images).
  • A detector that never saw caries can still flag them, but it cannot name them: pair with a classifier when a diagnosis is needed.

docs.title: Alternatives worth knowing
docs.text: Feature-space methods (PatchCore, k-NN on frozen DINOv3 patch tokens) beat reconstruction on many 2D benchmarks and need no training; latent-space distance with a JEPA encoder (jepa-pretraining) scales to 3D; diffusion restoration (AnoDDPM) gives sharper residuals at 100x the compute; for 3D volumes, a 3D VAE on patches or slice-wise 2D with aggregation.

docs.title: Building normal-only sets with pardesline
docs.text:
Healthy controls: ixi_brain_mri (healthy subjects, T1/T2/PD), hf_openmind (mostly healthy OpenNeuro cohorts), openneuro_ds000228; CT controls can be cut from totalsegmentator_ct regions without lesions; abnormal test cases: msd_task01_braintumour, hf_kits23 (tumours), luna16 (nodules). Split by patient, keep the licence.

scripts/vae_anomaly.py: 2D VAE (256 px) with beta warm-up, training on a folder of normal images, scoring of a folder with residual heatmaps (PNG) and image scores (CSV), evaluation (AUROC / AUPRC) when a labels file is given. Needs torch, pillow; runs a smoke test on synthetic images with --smoke.

Source: skills/vae-anomaly-detection/SKILL.md, published on 2026-10-14.

docs.title: Showcase: ten pipelines, one package
docs.text:
Each poster below is a real pipeline from PardesLine's work on 3D vision and medical imaging. Under every poster: what it does, the one-line way to run it with pardesline, the expert skill that explains it in depth, and the MCP tool an AI agent calls to get there. Everything runs on your machine with pip install "pardesline[all]"; nothing needs an account.

Three ways to use any of them:

You are Do this a Python developer import pardesline as pl, copy the snippet, run it an AI agent (Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Codex) pardesline mcp, then get_skill("<skill>") and the tools named below a reader the skill's SKILL.md is the written version of the poster, with the formulas and the failure modes

docs.title: 1. Beyond reconstruction: JEPA predicts in latent space
docs.text:
No decoder, no pixel reconstruction: a context encoder, an EMA target encoder and a predictor that learns only what is predictable - anatomy, not noise. The 3D reference trainer tokenises volumes from any pardesline dataset.

python skills/jepa-pretraining/scripts/jepa3d_pretrain.py --dataset totalsegmentator_ct --role ct --take 200 --crop 96
python skills/jepa-pretraining/scripts/jepa3d_pretrain.py --smoke        # CPU, seconds

Skill: jepa-pretraining. MCP: list_datasets(medical_only=true), get_skill("jepa-pretraining").

docs.title: 2. DINOv2 to DINOv3: why dense features stopped collapsing
docs.text:
Scaling broke patch-level features; one loss on the Gram matrix of patch similarities fixed it. Clean dense features at high resolution are the primitive geometric tasks are built on, and a frozen backbone is now a production design.

python skills/dinov3-dense-features/scripts/dinov3_features.py ./frames --out ./feats --size 512   # patch tokens + PCA maps

Skill: dinov3-dense-features. MCP: get_skill("dinov3-dense-features").

docs.title: 3. Frozen DINOv3 + Faster R-CNN on echocardiography
docs.text:
A backbone that never saw an ultrasound already separates myocardium, blood pool and pericardium; a 25 M-parameter head learns to name what it sees. ViTDet simple feature pyramid, RPN, RoIAlign, box head, NMS.

python skills/dinov3-dense-features/scripts/dinov3_faster_rcnn.py train --images ./echo --ann train.json --val-ann val.json --out ./runs/effusion

Skill: dinov3-dense-features (section "Heads on a frozen backbone"). MCP: get_skill("dinov3-dense-features", "scripts/dinov3_faster_rcnn.py").

docs.title: 4. From a point cloud to 3D Gaussian splats
docs.text:
Position, k-NN scale, identity rotation, logit opacity, SH degree-0 colour: five steps per point, a covariance that stays valid, a PLY that any 3DGS viewer opens.

python skills/gaussian-splatting/scripts/points_to_gaussians.py open3d_bunny bunny_splat.ply --colour 0.8 0.7 0.6

Verified: 100 000 Gaussians written and read back (24.8 MB, 62 floats each). Skill: gaussian-splatting; datasets c3vd_endoscopy_splats, hf_3d_arena, hf_kitti360_gs_subset. MCP: load_sample("c3vd_endoscopy_splats", 0, "splat").

docs.title: 5. Point clouds, meshes, voxels, Gaussian splats: which representation?
docs.text:
The representation decides memory, architecture and what is possible: points for LiDAR and scanners, meshes for surfaces and biomechanics, voxels for CT and MRI, splats for photorealistic rendering. pardesline keeps one typed object per kind and converts between them only where the conversion is well posed, recording every step.

import pardesline as pl

mask = pl.load("msd_task02_heart").filter(split="Tr")[0].mask  # label map, LPS mm
surface = mask.to_mesh(label=1)  # exact boundary
points = surface.to_points(num_points=4096)  # for a point network
field = surface.run("sdf.compute_sdf", voxel_size=1.0)  # implicit field

Skill: 3d-representations (conversion matrix, memory arithmetic, pitfalls). MCP: get_skill("3d-representations"), to_mesh, run_method.

docs.title: 6. From a labelled atlas to a segmented 3D-ultrasound heart
docs.text:
Register the atlas onto the scan, give every scan point the label of its nearest anatomical structure, reconstruct each chamber with Poisson, measure volumes in millilitres, evaluate against the truth.

aligned = scan.align(atlas)  # atlas moves, point order kept
# nearest-structure labels, per-label Poisson surfaces, volumes: scripts/atlas_label_transfer.py

Verified: 99.2 % label agreement and 0.04° pose error on a synthetic scan. Skill: atlas-label-transfer. MCP: get_skill("atlas-label-transfer", "scripts/atlas_label_transfer.py").

docs.title: 7. PointNet segmentation of CBCT point clouds
docs.text:
T-Net alignment, shared MLP, max-pool global feature, local + global concatenation, per-point softmax: the whole network, tensor by tensor, plus the data contract and how to build labelled clouds from any label map.

# label maps -> labelled clouds (.npz, unit sphere, normals, class table)
# python skills/pointnet-segmentation/scripts/make_point_dataset.py msd_task04_hippocampus --out ./hippo --take 20
# python skills/pointnet-segmentation/scripts/pointnet_seg.py train --data ./hippo --out ./runs/hippo

Skill: pointnet-segmentation. MCP: list_samples("msd_task04_hippocampus"), load_sample(..., "mask"), get_skill("pointnet-segmentation", "scripts/pointnet_seg.py").

docs.title: 8. Unsupervised caries detection with a variational autoencoder
docs.text:
A model trained only on healthy teeth cannot reconstruct a cavity; the residual map exposes it. Reconstruction + KL with beta warm-up, residual smoothing, thresholds from normal validation data, AUROC / AUPRC.

python skills/vae-anomaly-detection/scripts/vae_anomaly.py train --normal ./healthy --out ./runs/vae
python skills/vae-anomaly-detection/scripts/vae_anomaly.py score --weights ./runs/vae/vae.pt --images ./test --out ./scores

Skill: vae-anomaly-detection. MCP: get_skill("vae-anomaly-detection").

docs.title: 9. Rigid CT / MRI registration with SimpleITK
docs.text:
Two modalities with unrelated intensities need an information-theoretic metric: Mattes mutual information, a centred Euler transform, gradient descent with physical-shift scales and a multi-resolution pyramid. The result is validated by target registration error, never by the metric value alone.

s = pl.load("rire_brain")[0]  # CT + MR-T1 of one brain
moved = s.ct.align(s.mr_t1, metric="mattes_mutual_information", num_iterations=200)
moved.transform["rotation_deg"], moved.transform["translation_mm"]

Verified: scripts/rigid_ct_mr.py on the RIRE pair (3.9° rotation found, metric trace, checkerboard). Skill: multimodal-rigid-registration. MCP: load_sample("rire_brain", "training_001", "ct"), run_method("simpleitk_registration.rigid", ...).

docs.title: 10. RANSAC + ICP point-cloud registration
docs.text:
Global alignment on FPFH features with RANSAC, refinement with point-to-plane ICP, every parameter derived from one voxel size. The same pipeline that aligns LiDAR sweeps aligns an atlas onto a patient scan.

fixed = pl.load("scan.ply").with_frame("sensor", "mm")
moving = pl.load("atlas.ply").with_frame("sensor", "mm")
aligned = fixed.align(moving)  # registration.ransac_icp_pipeline
aligned.transform["fitness"], aligned.transform["inlier_rmse"]

Verified: scripts/registration_eval.py recovers a 35° synthetic transform on the bunny with 0.05° error. Skill: point-cloud-registration. MCP: run_method("registration.ransac_icp_pipeline", input_path, moving_path=...).

docs.title: The common ground
docs.text:
• Data: 43 datasets load in one line (pl.load("msd_task02_heart"), pl.load("tcia://Pancreas-CT"), pl.load("hf://org/name")), licence attached, nothing downloaded until you touch a sample.
  • Objects: a PointCloud, Mesh, Volume or LabelMap knows its frame, units, labels, licence and provenance; conversions are exact or say they are not.
  • Algorithms: 73, validated parameters, local or on the hosted GPU with the same names.
  • Libraries: Open3D, SimpleITK, PyVista are one call away (obj.to_open3d(), obj.to_sitk(), obj.to_pyvista()).
  • Agents: pardesline mcp gives all of it, plus these skills, to any MCP client without an account.
  • Metrics: evaluation-metrics-3d says which number to report and how.
